subproblems.statement: Appendix A.4 with the additional hypothesis (H0). Let P, n, Q ∈ ℕ, let F be a set of functions φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, and let sing be any map from functions ℝ^P → ℝ^Q to subsets of ℝ^P. Write φ_{y,λ}(x) := φ(y + λx), μH[n] for the (unnormalized) n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P, and say that a sequence φ_k converges weakly to φ if ∫ f·φ_k dμH[n] → ∫ f·φ dμH[n] for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Assume: (H0) two members of F that agree μH[n]-a.e. are equal; (H1) every φ ∈ F is locally μH[n]-integrable; (A.1) φ_{y,λ} ∈ F whenever φ ∈ F, 0 < λ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ; (A.2) for every φ ∈ F, every y with |y| < 1 and every strictly decreasing sequence λ_k > 0 with λ_k → 0, there are a strictly increasing sequence of indices k_i and ψ ∈ F such that φ_{y,λ_{k_i}} converges weakly to ψ and ψ(λx) = ψ(x) for all λ > 0 and all x; (A.3) for every φ ∈ F: sing φ is closed; sing φ = ∅ whenever φ = c·1_L for some c ∈ ℝ^Q and some n-dimensional linear subspace L; sing φ_{y,λ} = {x : y + λx ∈ sing φ} whenever 0 < λ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ; and whenever φ_k ∈ F converge weakly to φ, for every ε > 0 there is k₀ with B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_k ⊆ {x : dist(x, sing φ) < ε} for all k ≥ k₀ (the right side being empty if sing φ = ∅). Then either (I) B_1(0) ∩ sing φ = ∅ for every φ ∈ F, or (II) there is an integer d with 0 ≤ d ≤ n − 1 such that μH[d + α](sing φ ∩ B_1(0)) = 0 for every φ ∈ F and every real α > 0; there are ψ ∈ F and a d-dimensional linear subspace L with sing ψ = L and ψ(y + λx) = ψ(x) for all y ∈ L, λ > 0 and x; and, if d = 0, sing φ ∩ B_σ(0) is finite for every φ ∈ F and every σ < 1.

Then v(M, θ) is stationary in N ∩ U: ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n = 0 for every X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^P) with X(x) ∈ T_xN for all x ∈ N ∩ U (R.IsStationaryAlong N).

Source: Simon 7.1.2 and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 29–60) with README erratum 1, i.e. steps 1 and 3–5 of the parent proof; the hypothesis H^n(M ∖ N) = 0 is the consequence of spt T ⊆ N established in step 2 of the parent proof (sibling imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null). Siblings used: imrep_represents_massOn_eq_measure (MASS), imrep_c1_diffeo_pushforward_im (PUSH), tangential_c1_deformation_exists (DEFORM), pushforward_action_massOn_le_first_variation (EXPAND).
1. Fix X ∈ C¹(ℝ^P; ℝ^P) with compact support, tsupport X ⊆ U and X(x) ∈ tangentSpace N x for x ∈ N ∩ U. Put K := tsupport X (compact, ⊆ U) and δV(X) := R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n. We show δV(X) = 0.
2. Case n = 0. approxTangentPlane 0 M x has finrank 0, hence equals ⊥, for every x (in both branches of its definition), so its projection is 0 and tangentialDivergence 0 M X x = trace 0 = 0; thus δV(X) = 0. (This is consistent with step 1 of the parent proof, which shows moreover M = ∅.) Assume n ≥ 1 from now on.
3. Choice of W. As K is compact in the open U, there is an open W with K ⊆ W, closure W compact and closure W ⊆ U (a small open thickening of K). Then R.measure W ≤ ∫_{M∩closure W} θ dH^n < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult), and by MASS, T.massOn W = R.measure W. Put m := (R.measure W).toReal, so R.measure W = ofReal m.
4. Degenerate case m = 0. Then H^n(M ∩ W) = 0 (θ ≥ 1 on M). For x ∉ K, DX(x) = 0 (X vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K), so tangentialDivergence n M X x = 0. Hence the integrand of δV(X) vanishes H^n⌞M-a.e. and δV(X) = 0. Assume m > 0.
5. Deformations. DEFORM (applied to U, N, X) gives φ : ℝ → ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that for every t: φ_t is C¹, bijective, with injective derivative, φ_t = id off K and φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U; and (D): for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 with ‖Dφ_t(x) − I − tDX(x)‖ ≤ ε|t| for all |t| < δ and all x. Since φ_t is a bijection fixing every point of ℝ^P ∖ K, it maps ℝ^P ∖ K onto itself and hence K onto K.
6. Competitors. For each t, PUSH (with U, T, R, K and φ_t) gives an integer multiplicity S_t ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with BoundaryVanishes S_t (because BoundaryVanishes T) and S_t(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω(φ_t x)∘Dφ_t(x)) dH^n for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U).
7. S_t is admissible in 7.1.1 with this W. (a) W is open and CompactlyContained W U; S_t is integer multiplicity. (b) SameBoundary S_t T: n ≥ 1 and S_t.boundary = 0 = T.boundary. (c) spt(S_t − T) ⊆ K ∩ N. K ∩ N is compact: N ∩ U = N̄ ∩ U by (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, so K ∩ N = K ∩ N̄ is closed in the compact K. Let y ∈ U ∖ (K ∩ N); choose r > 0 with closedBall(y, r) ⊆ U and closedBall(y, r) ∩ K ∩ N = ∅, and W_y := ball(y, r) (open, closure compact ⊆ U). For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W_y, using T ω = R.action ω: (S_t − T)(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)[ξ(x)(ω(φ_t x)∘Dφ_t(x)) − ξ(x)(ω(x))] dH^n; the two integrals may be merged because both integrands are integrable (each is a.e. strongly measurable and bounded by C·θ on a compact subset of U — φ_t^{-1}(tsupport ω), resp. tsupport ω — and vanishes elsewhere, |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ a.e.; R.locallyIntegrable_mult). The bracket vanishes for x ∈ M ∖ K (φ_t = id on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K, so φ_t x = x and Dφ_t(x) = I); it vanishes for x ∈ M ∩ K ∩ N, because x and φ_t(x) both lie in K ∩ N (step 5: φ_t(K) = K, φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U) where ω vanishes; and M ∩ K ∖ N is H^n-null by hypothesis. So S_t − T vanishes on W_y and y ∈ zeroRegion(S_t − T). Hence spt(S_t − T) ⊆ K ∩ N ⊆ (N ∩ U) ∩ W. (d) spt(S_t − T) is compact: it is relatively closed in U (complement of the open zeroRegion) and contained in the compact set K ∩ N ⊆ U, so it equals (K ∩ N) ∩ F for a closed F.
   Therefore IsMinimizingIn T (N ∩ U) gives T.massOn W ≤ S_t.massOn W, i.e. ofReal m ≤ S_t.massOn W, for every t ∈ ℝ.
8. First variation bound. EXPAND (with W open, R.measure W ≠ ∞, X C¹ with compact support, K ⊆ W, φ_t C¹, φ_t = id off K, and (D)) gives: for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that S_t.massOn W ≤ ofReal(m + t·δV(X) + ε|t|) for all |t| < δ (S_t satisfies the action formula required there).
9. Conclusion. Suppose a := δV(X) ≠ 0. Take ε := |a|/2, δ from step 8, and t := −s·sign(a) with 0 < s < δ and s|a|/2 < m. Then m + ta + ε|t| = m − s|a|/2 ∈ (0, m), and steps 7–8 give ofReal m ≤ S_t.massOn W ≤ ofReal(m − s|a|/2) < ofReal m, a contradiction. Hence δV(X) = R.firstVariation X = 0. As X was arbitrary, R.IsStationaryAlong N.
proof_key_steps: n = 0 is trivial (0-dimensional approximate tangent planes); otherwise fix X tangent to N and W ⊂⊂ U containing spt X, with M_W(T) = μ_V(W).
The deformations φ_t (DEFORM) push T forward to integer multiplicity competitors S_t (PUSH) with ∂S_t = 0 and spt(S_t − T) ⊆ spt X ∩ N compact, using H^n(M ∖ N) = 0.
Minimality gives μ_V(W) ≤ M_W(S_t) ≤ μ_V(W) + tδV(X) + ε|t| (EXPAND) for all small t of both signs, forcing δV(X) = 0.

Source: proof of Simon 7.3.1, displays (1) and (4) and the sentence after (4) (chapter-07.txt lines 329–341); step 5 of the parent proof. Uses the siblings mass_eq_measure (M) and blowup_scaling (BU). Write η_j := η_{x,λ_j}, S_j := η_{j#}T, ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞) and a(ρ) := ω_nρⁿθ (θ ≥ 0 by HasMassDensity).
1. Representations. Let R represent T and R_C represent C. By BU(2), for each j there is a representation R_j of S_j with μ_{R_j}(B) = λ_j^{−n}μ_R(η_j⁻¹(B)) for Borel B. Applying MassMeasuresConverge to (R_j) and R_C: ∫f dμ_{R_j} → ∫f dμ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), where μ := μ_{R_C}. μ is finite on bounded sets (local integrability of R_C).
2. Book (1). For ρ > 0, η_j⁻¹(B_ρ(0)) = B_{λ_jρ}(x), so μ_{R_j}(B_ρ(0)) = λ_j^{−n}μ_R(B_{λ_jρ}(x)). For j large, B_{λ_jρ}(x) ⊆ U, and M gives μ_R(B_{λ_jρ}(x)) = M_{B_{λ_jρ}(x)}(T). Hence μ_{R_j}(B_ρ(0)) = ω_nρⁿ·M_{B_{λ_jρ}(x)}(T)/(ω_n(λ_jρ)ⁿ) → ω_nρⁿθ = a(ρ), because λ_jρ ↓ 0 and HasMassDensity T x θ.
3. Book (4). Let ρ > 0 with μ(∂B_ρ(0)) = 0. (i) For a compact F ⊆ B_ρ(0) choose f ∈ C_c(B_ρ(0)) with 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f = 1 on F; then μ(F) ≤ ∫f dμ = lim∫f dμ_{R_j} ≤ liminf μ_{R_j}(B_ρ(0)); by inner regularity of the finite measure μ⌞B_ρ(0), μ(B_ρ(0)) ≤ liminf μ_{R_j}(B_ρ(0)). (ii) For δ > 0 choose g ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, g = 1 on closedBall(0, ρ), spt g ⊆ B_{ρ+δ}(0); then lim sup μ_{R_j}(B_ρ(0)) ≤ lim ∫g dμ_{R_j} = ∫g dμ ≤ μ(B_{ρ+δ}(0)), and letting δ ↓ 0, lim sup μ_{R_j}(B_ρ(0)) ≤ μ(closedBall(0, ρ)) = μ(B_ρ(0)). So μ_{R_j}(B_ρ(0)) → μ(B_ρ(0)), and with step 2, μ(B_ρ(0)) = a(ρ).
4. The spheres ∂B_ρ(0), ρ > 0, are pairwise disjoint and μ is finite on each closedBall(0, m); hence μ(∂B_ρ(0)) > 0 for at most countably many ρ, and the set D of ρ > 0 with μ(∂B_ρ(0)) = 0 is dense in (0, ∞). For arbitrary ρ > 0 choose ρ_i ∈ D with ρ_i ↑ ρ; B_ρ(0) = ⋃_i B_{ρ_i}(0), so by continuity from below and step 3, μ(B_ρ(0)) = lim μ(B_{ρ_i}(0)) = lim a(ρ_i) = a(ρ) ("by monotonicity in ρ and left-continuity").
5. By M (U = ℝ^P), M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = μ(B_ρ(0)) = ω_nρⁿθ = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(ρⁿ) · ofReal θ for every ρ > 0.
6. HasMassDensity C 0 θ: θ ≥ 0, and for every ρ > 0, M_{B_ρ(0)}(C)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)) = ofReal θ because ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ) ∈ (0, ∞); so the quotient is constant on (0, ∞) and tends to ofReal θ as ρ ↓ 0.
proof_key_steps: Push a representation of T forward to the blow-ups (blowup_scaling) and feed it into MassMeasuresConverge.
Scaling: μ_{S_j}(B_ρ(0)) = λ_j^{−n}M_{B_{λ_jρ}(x)}(T) → ω_nρⁿθ (book (1)).
Weak convergence of measures gives μ_{S_j}(B_ρ(0)) → μ_C(B_ρ(0)) whenever μ_C(∂B_ρ(0)) = 0 (book (4)); left continuity extends the identity to all ρ.
mass_eq_measure converts to M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = ω_nρⁿθ, and the constant quotient gives HasMassDensity C 0 θ.

subproblems.title: A stationary integer multiplicity cycle with constant density ratio at 0 is a cone (Simon 7.3.1 proof, lines 347–355) (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, n ≥ 1 and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) integer multiplicity with ∂C = 0, such that for every integer multiplicity representation R = (M, θ, ξ) of C the varifold v(M, θ) is stationary in ℝ^P (R.IsStationaryAlong univ), and suppose there is θ₀ ∈ ℝ with M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = ω_n·ρⁿ·θ₀ (as unitBallVolume n · ofReal(ρⁿ) · ofReal θ₀) for every ρ > 0. Then C is a cone: η_{0,λ#}C = C for every λ > 0 (IsConeCurrent C, i.e. currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(ω) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P)).

Source: proof of Simon 7.3.1, lines 336–360 (chapter-07.txt: stationarity of V_C (3), the monotonicity formula 3.6 of Ch. 4 giving D^⊥r = 0, x ∧ C⃗ = 0, and Lemma 2.33 of Ch. 6), and Simon Ch. 6, 2.25–2.27 and 2.33 (chapter-06.txt lines 441–470, 557–569); step 6 of the parent proof. Uses the sibling mass_eq_measure (M). Let R = (M, θ, ξ) represent C, μ := μ_R, a := ω_n·max(θ₀, 0) (so the hypothesis reads M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = aρⁿ), r(y) := |y|; for y ∈ M where T_yM exists, p_y is the orthogonal projection onto T_yM and div_M X(y) = trace(p_y∘DX(y)).
0. The first variation is a genuine Lebesgue integral. For increasing (n−1)-indices J let e^J be the basic (n−1)-covector (for n = 1, e^∅ = 1), and for v ∈ ℝ^P let v^♭ ∧ e^J be the n-covector (u₁,…,uₙ) ↦ Σ_b (−1)^{b−1}⟨v, u_b⟩e^J(u₁,…,û_b,…,uₙ). If ζ(α) = ±α(τ₁,…,τₙ) for an orthonormal frame τ of an n-dimensional subspace Q, then Σ_J ζ(v^♭∧e^J)ζ(w^♭∧e^J) = Σ_{b,b'}(−1)^{b+b'}⟨v,τ_b⟩⟨w,τ_{b'}⟩Σ_J e^J(τ_{≠b})e^J(τ_{≠b'}) = Σ_b⟨v,τ_b⟩⟨w,τ_b⟩ = ⟨p_Q v, w⟩, because by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_J e^J(τ_{≠b})e^J(τ_{≠b'}) is the determinant of the Gram matrix (⟨τ_i, τ_{i'}⟩)_{i≠b, i'≠b'}, which is 1 if b = b' and 0 otherwise (if b ≠ b', the row of τ_{b'} vanishes). Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M the orthogonal projection p_y onto T_yM = approxTangentPlane n M y (which exists and is unique a.e. by the field `orients` and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) equals Π(ξ(y)), where Π(ζ) is the linear map with ⟨Π(ζ)v, w⟩ = Σ_J ζ(v^♭∧e^J)ζ(w^♭∧e^J), a continuous (quadratic) function of ζ. So y ↦ p_y is a.e. strongly measurable on M, and for a C¹ field X with compact support the function y ↦ θ(y)·trace(p_y∘DX(y)) (= θ·tangentialDivergence n M X) is a.e. strongly measurable and bounded by n·sup‖DX‖·θ·1_{spt X}, which is integrable on M because spt X is a compact set. Thus R.firstVariation X = ∫ div_M X dμ is the integral of an integrable function, and the first-variation hypothesis is a genuine identity of integrals.
1. By M (U = ℝ^P), μ(B_ρ(0)) = aρⁿ for every ρ > 0. As closedBall(0, ρ) = ⋂_{ρ'>ρ} B_{ρ'}(0) and μ(B_{ρ+1}(0)) < ∞, μ(closedBall(0, ρ)) = lim_{ρ'↓ρ} aρ'ⁿ = aρⁿ; and μ({0}) = lim_{ρ↓0} aρⁿ = 0 since n ≥ 1.
2. Stationarity. By hypothesis R.IsStationaryAlong univ: ∫ div_M X dμ = R.firstVariation X = 0 for every C¹ X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support (the tangency condition X(y) ∈ T_y ℝ^P is vacuous: tangentSpace univ y contains every v, via γ(t) = y + tv), the integral being genuine by step 0.
3. Monotonicity identity (Ch. 4, 3.1–3.6 with ξ = 0, R = ∞, H = 0). For ε ∈ (0, 1) let φ_ε be as in Ch. 4, 3.5 (C¹, nonincreasing, = 1 on (−∞, 1], = 0 on [1 + ε, ∞)). Testing step 2 with X(y) = φ_ε(r/ρ)y gives, exactly as in Ch. 4, 3.2–3.4, d/dρ(ρ^{−n}I(ρ)) = ρ^{−n}J'(ρ) with I(ρ) = ∫φ_ε(r/ρ) dμ, J(ρ) = ∫φ_ε(r/ρ)|D^⊥r|² dμ, D^⊥r(y) := (Id − p_y)(y/|y|) for y ≠ 0 (I, J are C¹ by differentiation under the integral sign; the point 0 is μ-null by step 1). Integrating from σ to ρ and using that ∂_tφ_ε(r/t) ≥ 0 is supported in {r/(1+ε) ≤ t ≤ r}, where t^{−n} lies between r^{−n} and (1+ε)ⁿr^{−n}, gives Ch. 4, 3.5: ∫ r^{−n}(φ_ε(r/ρ) − φ_ε(r/σ))|D^⊥r|² dμ ≤ ρ^{−n}I(ρ) − σ^{−n}I(σ) ≤ (1+ε)ⁿ∫ r^{−n}(φ_ε(r/ρ) − φ_ε(r/σ))|D^⊥r|² dμ (the integrands vanish where r ≤ σ, so r^{−n} ≤ σ^{−n} on their supports). Letting ε ↓ 0 (dominated convergence) yields Ch. 4, 3.6: for 0 < σ < ρ, ρ^{−n}μ(closedBall(0, ρ)) − σ^{−n}μ(closedBall(0, σ)) = ∫_{closedBall(0,ρ) ∖ closedBall(0,σ)} |D^⊥r|²r^{−n} dμ.
4. By step 1 the left side of 3.6 is a − a = 0. Hence |D^⊥r|²r^{−n} = 0 μ-a.e. on every annulus closedBall(0, ρ) ∖ closedBall(0, σ), so D^⊥r = 0 μ-a.e. on ℝ^P ∖ {0} (countable union of annuli), and μ-a.e. on ℝ^P as μ({0}) = 0. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, this means: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M, y ∈ T_yM.
5. "x ∧ C⃗ = 0 μ_C-a.e." For Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M, ξ(y)(α) = ±α(τ₁, …, τₙ) with τ an orthonormal basis of T_yM (field `orients`) and y ∈ T_yM (step 4). Lemma U (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2)). Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^P (Euclid P) with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, and let A ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set with μ(ℝ^P ∖ A) = 0. Then for μHE[n]-almost every x ∈ ℝ^P with x ∉ A, μ(B̄_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρ)ⁿ → 0 in [0, ∞] as ρ ↓ 0, where B̄_ρ(x) is the closed ball.
Proof of Lemma U.
Source: Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2), the fact "the upper density vanishes Hⁿ-a.e. off the carrier" cited in parent step 3(iii). The printed proof is reproduced for a locally finite Borel measure: density comparison (Ch. 1, 3.2) via the Vitali covering lemma (Ch. 1, 3.3), inner regularity by closed sets, then localization.

The same argument, written for μ = μHE[n]⌞S with μHE[n](S) < ∞, is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.regcomp_atl_upper_density_zero of DAG node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.approx_tangent_locality-a1.upper_density_zero-a1 (candidate 031b5125695febe04a82aacb729a15164ef02960). These accepted declarations are reading references only. They are not dependencies of this child and are not in its worktree, and the numbered proof below is self-contained. Their Lean proofs show the same Vitali and comparison steps with μHE[n](S ∩ ·) in place of λ(·); Submission.regcomp_atl_local_density_zero shows the localization by balls. The SimonGMT lemmas simon_theorem_3_6 and simon_remark_3_7_of_openSigmaFinite are not used: they live in Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean, which the frozen header does not import.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] with c_n := addHaarScalarFactor(volume, μH[n]) ∈ (0, ∞) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, Measure.addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero). So Hⁿ and μH[n] have the same null sets. For a measure λ, x ∈ ℝ^P and ρ > 0 put r_λ(x, ρ) := λ(B̄_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρ)ⁿ ∈ [0, ∞]; ofReal(ρ)ⁿ ∈ (0, ∞) for ρ > 0.

U1. (Comparison lemma, Simon 3.2 with the crude constant 6ⁿ.) Let λ be a Borel measure, G a Borel set with λ(G) < ∞, t ∈ (0, ∞) and E ⊆ ℝ^P. Assume that for every x ∈ E and every δ > 0 there is ρ ∈ (0, δ) with t·ofReal(ρ)ⁿ ≤ λ(G ∩ B̄_ρ(x)). Then t·μH[n](E) ≤ 6ⁿ·λ(G).
Proof. Fix j ∈ ℕ and put δ_j := 1/(j + 1).
(a) Vitali selection. Consider the family of pairs a = (x_a, ρ_a) with x_a ∈ E, 0 < ρ_a < δ_j and t·ofReal(ρ_a)ⁿ ≤ λ(G ∩ B̄_{ρ_a}(x_a)), with the closed balls B̄_{ρ_a}(x_a) (nonempty) and radii ρ_a ≤ δ_j. Mathlib's Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement with τ = 2 gives a pairwise disjoint subfamily u_j such that every ball of the family meets some ball b ∈ u_j with ρ_a ≤ 2ρ_b. The balls of u_j are disjoint with nonempty interior, so u_j is countable (Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_nonempty_interior).
(b) Covering. For x ∈ E the hypothesis with δ = δ_j gives a member a = (x, ρ) of the family. Let b ∈ u_j be a ball meeting B̄_ρ(x) at a point w, with ρ ≤ 2ρ_b. Then |x − x_b| ≤ |x − w| + |w − x_b| ≤ ρ + ρ_b ≤ 3ρ_b. So E ⊆ ⋃_{b∈u_j} B̄_{3ρ_b}(x_b), and diam B̄_{3ρ_b}(x_b) ≤ 6ρ_b ≤ 6δ_j (ediam_le_of_forall_dist_le).
(c) Packing. By disjointness,
t·Σ_{b∈u_j} ofReal(ρ_b)ⁿ ≤ Σ_{b∈u_j} λ(G ∩ B̄_{ρ_b}(x_b)) = λ(⋃_{b∈u_j} G ∩ B̄_{ρ_b}(x_b)) ≤ λ(G)
(measure_biUnion). Hence t·Σ_{b∈u_j} diam(B̄_{3ρ_b}(x_b))ⁿ ≤ 6ⁿ·λ(G) for every j.
(d) Limit. Mathlib's MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum applies to the covers {B̄_{3ρ_b}(x_b) : b ∈ u_j} of E, whose diameters are ≤ 6δ_j → 0. It gives μH[n](E) ≤ liminf_j Σ_{b∈u_j} diam(B̄_{3ρ_b}(x_b))ⁿ ≤ 6ⁿλ(G)/t (ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le with t ∉ {0, ∞}). Multiplying by t gives the claim. For n = 0 the same computation holds with every n-th power equal to 1.

U2. (Finite measures.) Let λ be a finite Borel measure and A′ a Borel set with λ(A′ᶜ) = 0. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ A′, r_λ(x, ρ) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
Proof.
(a) Thresholds. For t ∈ (0, ∞) let N_t := {x : x ∉ A′ and t < r_λ(x, ρ) for ρ frequently in 𝓝[>]0}. Suppose x ∉ A′ and r_λ(x, ·) does not tend to 0. By ENNReal.tendsto_nhds_zero there is ε > 0 with ε < r_λ(x, ρ) frequently. Choosing k with 1/(k + 1) < ε (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt) gives x ∈ N_{1/(k+1)}. By measure_iUnion_null it therefore suffices to show Hⁿ(N_t) = 0 for every t ∈ (0, ∞), and for that it suffices to show μH[n](N_t) = 0.
(b) Fix t and ε′ ∈ (0, ∞). The finite Borel measure λ on the metric space ℝ^P is weakly regular (Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure). MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt (the current name of the deprecated exists_isClosed_diff_lt) gives a closed F ⊆ A′ with λ(A′ ∖ F) < t·ε′/6ⁿ. Put G := A′ ∖ F; it is Borel and λ(G) < ∞.
(c) Let x ∈ N_t and δ > 0. Then x ∉ F, since F ⊆ A′. As F is closed, some r₁ > 0 has B_{r₁}(x) ∩ F = ∅. Since the threshold holds frequently and ρ ∈ (0, min(δ, r₁/2)) holds eventually in 𝓝[>]0, pick ρ satisfying both (Frequently.and_eventually). Then B̄_ρ(x) ∩ F = ∅. As λ(A′ᶜ) = 0, λ(B̄_ρ(x)) = λ(A′ ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = λ(G ∩ B̄_ρ(x)). From t < r_λ(x, ρ) and 0 < ofReal(ρ)ⁿ < ∞ (ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt) we get t·ofReal(ρ)ⁿ < λ(G ∩ B̄_ρ(x)).
(d) Step U1 with E := N_t gives t·μH[n](N_t) ≤ 6ⁿλ(G) < 6ⁿ·(tε′/6ⁿ) = tε′. Hence μH[n](N_t) < ε′. As ε′ > 0 is arbitrary, μH[n](N_t) = 0, and Hⁿ(N_t) = c_n·0 = 0.

U3. (Localization; the statement.) For j ∈ ℕ let λ_j := μ.restrict (A ∩ B_j(0)), where B_j(0) is the open ball.
- λ_j is finite: λ_j(ℝ^P) = μ(A ∩ B_j(0)) ≤ μ(B̄_j(0)) < ∞, as B̄_j(0) is compact.
- λ_j((A ∩ B_j(0))ᶜ) = 0.
By step U2 for each j and ae_all_iff, Hⁿ-a.e. x satisfies: for every j, if x ∉ A ∩ B_j(0) then r_{λ_j}(x, ρ) → 0.
Fix such an x with x ∉ A. Choose j ∈ ℕ with |x| < j and put ε := (j − |x|)/2 > 0, so B̄_ε(x) ⊆ B_j(0). For 0 < ρ < ε, since μ(Aᶜ) = 0,
μ(B̄_ρ(x)) = μ(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = μ(A ∩ B_j(0) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = λ_j(B̄_ρ(x)).
So r_μ(x, ρ) = r_{λ_j}(x, ρ) on (0, ε), a set in 𝓝[>]0. Since x ∉ A ∩ B_j(0), r_{λ_j}(x, ·) → 0, and therefore r_μ(x, ρ) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0 (Tendsto.congr′). This holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ A, which is the claim. ∎

Main argument.
Notation.
- Hⁿ := μHE[n].
- ω_n := unitBallVolume n = volume(B_1(0) ⊆ Euclid n) ∈ (0, ∞): a nonempty bounded open set under Lebesgue measure; for n = 0 it equals 1.
- M′ := M ∩ W, a Borel set.
- μ := R.measure.restrict W, so μ(B) = R.measure(B ∩ W) = ∫_{M′∩B} θ dHⁿ for Borel B.
- ν := Hⁿ.restrict M′.
- q(x, ρ) := μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)) for ρ > 0.
Since balls are Borel, R.measure(B_ρ(x) ∩ W) = μ(B_ρ(x)) (Measure.restrict_apply). Also 1_{M′}(x)θ(x) = Set.indicator (R.carrier ∩ W) (fun y ↦ (R.mult y : ℝ≥0∞)) x. So the claim is: q(x, ρ) → 1_{M′}(x)θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x.

1. (Local finiteness and concentration.)
- μ(K) = R.measure(K ∩ W) < ∞ for every compact K, by hypothesis.
- θ ≥ 1 on M, so ν(B) = Hⁿ(M′ ∩ B) ≤ ∫_{M′∩B} θ dHⁿ = μ(B) for Borel B; in particular ν(K) < ∞ for compact K.
- R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ vanishes off M, and μ vanishes off W, so μ(M′ᶜ) = 0. Likewise ν(M′ᶜ) = 0.
- For ρ ≥ 0, ofReal(ρⁿ) = ofReal(ρ)ⁿ (ENNReal.ofReal_pow), and B_ρ(x) ⊆ B̄_ρ(x). Hence, for every measure λ, λ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)) ≤ ω_n⁻¹·λ(B̄_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρ)ⁿ.
 (†) So the open-ball ratio, normalized by ω_n, tends to 0 whenever the closed-ball ratio λ(B̄_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρ)ⁿ does.

2. (Off the carrier.) Apply Lemma U (Step 0) to the measure μ and the Borel set M′. Its hypotheses hold by step 1. It gives an Hⁿ-null set E₀ such that for x ∉ M′ ∪ E₀, μ(B̄_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρ)ⁿ → 0. By (†), q(x, ρ) → 0 = 1_{M′}(x)θ(x).

3. (Unit density at approximate-tangent points; Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3).) By the IMRep field orients, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q (in particular finrank Q = n). By definition this means: ∫_{blowUpMap x ρ '' M} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as ρ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), where blowUpMap x ρ (p) = ρ⁻¹(p − x). Let E′ ⊆ M be the Hⁿ-null set of points of M where this fails. Fix x ∈ M′ ∖ E′, the subspace Q, and δ > 0 with B_{2δ}(x) ⊆ W (W is open). Write η_ρ := blowUpMap x ρ. Claim: ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)) → 1.
(a) Scaling. For every set A, Hⁿ(η_ρ(A)) = ofReal(ρ⁻¹)ⁿ·Hⁿ(A). Indeed η_ρ(A) = ρ⁻¹ • (A − x). The translation y ↦ y − x is an isometry, so it preserves Hⁿ (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image applied to (IsometryEquiv.subRight x).isometry), and Hⁿ(c • B) = ‖c‖₊ⁿ·Hⁿ(B) for c ≠ 0 (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). This combination compiles after import GMT.Ch07.Submission. (MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image concerns y ↦ x + c(y − x) and can also be used after rewriting.)
(b) For 0 < ρ < δ, M ∩ B_{2ρ}(x) = M′ ∩ B_{2ρ}(x). Hence:
 - η_ρ(M) ∩ B_2(0) = η_ρ(M′ ∩ B_{2ρ}(x));
 - Hⁿ(η_ρ(M) ∩ B_1(0)) = ofReal(ρ)⁻ⁿ·ν(B_ρ(x));
 - Hⁿ(η_ρ(M) ∩ B_2(0)) = ofReal(ρ)⁻ⁿ·ν(B_{2ρ}(x)) < ∞.
(c) Fix 0 < ε < 1 and take continuous f^±: ℝ^P → [0, 1] with compact support:
 - f⁺(p) := min(1, max(0, (1 + ε − |p|)/ε)), which is 1 on B̄_1(0) and 0 off B_{1+ε}(0) ⊆ B_2(0);
 - f⁻(p) := min(1, max(0, (1 − |p|)/ε)), which is 1 on B̄_{1−ε}(0) and 0 off B_1(0).
 Both are integrable over η_ρ(M), since they are bounded and supported in B_2(0), which has finite measure by (b). As 1_{B_1(0)} lies between f⁻ and f⁺, the following holds as real numbers. All quantities are finite by (b), and the measure values are compared through toReal.
 ∫_{η_ρ(M)} f⁻ dHⁿ ≤ (Hⁿ(η_ρ(M) ∩ B_1(0))).toReal = (ofReal(ρ)⁻ⁿ·ν(B_ρ(x))).toReal ≤ ∫_{η_ρ(M)} f⁺ dHⁿ.
(d) Hⁿ(Q ∩ B_t(0)) = ω_n·tⁿ for t > 0. Indeed, Q with the induced inner product is an n-dimensional inner product space, and the inclusion Q → ℝ^P is an isometry (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). Hⁿ on Q is its volume (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume with finrank Q = n). An orthonormal basis gives a linear isometry Q ≃ Euclid n, which preserves volume. In Euclid n the ball of radius t > 0 has volume ofReal(tⁿ)·ω_n (Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos, which needs no nontriviality, so n = 0 is included). Since 1_{B̄_{1−ε}(0)} ≤ f⁻ and f⁺ ≤ 1_{B_{1+ε}(0)},
 ω_n(1 − ε)ⁿ ≤ ∫_Q f⁻ dHⁿ and ∫_Q f⁺ dHⁿ ≤ ω_n(1 + ε)ⁿ.
(e) Let ρ ↓ 0 in (c), using the approximate-tangent convergence for f^±. This gives
 ω_n(1 − ε)ⁿ ≤ liminf ν(B_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρⁿ) ≤ limsup ν(B_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρⁿ) ≤ ω_n(1 + ε)ⁿ.
 Then let ε ↓ 0 and divide by ω_n ∈ (0, ∞); this proves the claim.

4. (Density θ on the carrier; Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8.) For m ≥ 1 let M′_m := {p ∈ M′ : θ(p) = m} and A_m := M′ ∖ M′_m; both are Borel. Since θ is ℕ-valued and ≥ 1 on M, M′ = ⋃_{m≥1} M′_m (disjoint union).
Fix m. The measures μ.restrict A_m and ν.restrict A_m are finite on compact sets (step 1) and vanish off A_m. Apply Lemma U (Step 0) to each of them with the set A_m. This gives an Hⁿ-null set E_m such that, for x ∉ A_m ∪ E_m:
 μ(A_m ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρ)ⁿ → 0 and ν(A_m ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρ)ⁿ → 0.
By (†), the corresponding open-ball ratios normalized by ω_n also tend to 0.
Now let x ∈ M′_m ∖ (E_m ∪ E′); note M′_m ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ A_m. For ρ ∈ (0, δ) all terms below are finite, and
 μ(B_ρ(x)) = μ(M′_m ∩ B_ρ(x)) + μ(A_m ∩ B_ρ(x))
 = m·ν(M′_m ∩ B_ρ(x)) + μ(A_m ∩ B_ρ(x))
 = m·[ν(B_ρ(x)) − ν(A_m ∩ B_ρ(x))] + μ(A_m ∩ B_ρ(x)).
The first equality holds because μ vanishes off M′ = M′_m ∪ A_m; the second because θ = m on M′_m. Dividing by ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ) and using step 3 together with the two vanishing ratios gives q(x, ρ) → m·1 − m·0 + 0 = m = θ(x) = 1_{M′}(x)θ(x). This is arithmetic of finite limits, for example after passing to toReal.

5. (Conclusion.) The set E₀ ∪ E′ ∪ ⋃_{m≥1} E_m is Hⁿ-null (countable union). Outside it, q(x, ρ) → 1_{M′}(x)θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0: by step 2 if x ∉ M′, and by step 4 with m = θ(x) if x ∈ M′. ∎
proof_key_steps: Lemma U (Simon 1.3.6, 3.7(2)): Vitali comparison t·μH[n](E) ≤ 6ⁿλ(G), inner regularity by closed sets for finite measures, and localization to balls give vanishing upper density Hⁿ-a.e. off a set carrying a locally finite measure.
μ := R.measure⌞W and ν := Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ W) are finite on compact sets (θ ≥ 1 on M) and concentrated on M′ = M ∩ W; open-ball ratios normalized by ω_n are bounded by closed-ball ratios.
Off M′: Lemma U applied to (μ, M′) gives zero density Hⁿ-a.e. off M′.
At Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M′ the carrier has an approximate tangent plane Q. Testing with cut-offs of B_1(0), using Hⁿ(η_{x,ρ}A) = ρ^{−n}Hⁿ(A) and Hⁿ(Q ∩ B_t) = ω_ntⁿ, gives ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) → 1.
Split M′ into the Borel level sets {θ = m}. Lemma U applied to μ⌞A_m and ν⌞A_m, with A_m = M′ ∖ {θ = m}, makes the other levels negligible, so the ratio tends to m = θ(x) at Hⁿ-a.e. point of {θ = m}.
The countable union of exceptional sets is Hⁿ-null.

An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U consists of a Borel set M ⊆ U that is countably n-rectifiable, a measurable θ : ℝ^P → ℕ with θ > 0 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and ξ : ℝ^P → Λₙ(ℝ^P), a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, such that for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q. R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(y)·ξ(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y); R represents T iff T(ω) = R.action(ω) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); μ_R = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density θ (IMRep.measure).
1. η is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse ι: η is y ↦ λ⁻¹y (a homeomorphism, λ⁻¹ ≠ 0) followed by the translation z ↦ z − λ⁻¹x, η(ι(z)) = λ⁻¹(x + λz − x) = z and ι(η(y)) = x + λ·λ⁻¹(y − x) = y. Hence η is a measurable embedding (a Borel isomorphism of ℝ^P): η maps Borel sets onto Borel sets, η⁻¹(η(s)) = s and η(η⁻¹(t)) = t for all sets s, t.
2. Key identity: for every Borel s, Hⁿ⌞η(s) = c·η_#(Hⁿ⌞s). Proof: for a measurable embedding η, every measure ν and every set t, (η_#ν)⌞t = η_#(ν⌞η⁻¹(t)) (Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map). With ν = Hⁿ and t = η(s): η_#(Hⁿ⌞s) = (η_#Hⁿ)⌞η(s) = (ofReal(λⁿ)·Hⁿ)⌞η(s) = ofReal(λⁿ)·(Hⁿ⌞η(s)) by hausdorff_scaling (ii). Since c·ofReal(λⁿ) = ofReal(λ^{−n}λⁿ) = 1, multiplying by c gives the claim. Consequences, for Borel s:
 (A) for g : ℝ^P → [0,∞], ∫_{η(s)} g dHⁿ = c·∫_s g∘η dHⁿ (lintegral against a scalar multiple of a measure, and MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map, which needs no measurability of g);
 (B) for g : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{η(s)} g dHⁿ = λ^{−n}·∫_s g∘η dHⁿ for the Bochner integral (integral_smul_measure with c.toReal = λ^{−n}, and MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, which holds for every g, integrable or not);
 (C) if a property q satisfies q(η(y)) for Hⁿ⌞s-a.e. y, then q holds Hⁿ⌞η(s)-a.e. (MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff; a ν-null set is (c·ν)-null);
 (D) if h∘η is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞s, then h is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞η(s) (MeasurableEmbedding.aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff and AEStronglyMeasurable.smul_measure).
3. Definition of R' and verification of the IMRep conditions in η(U). Let R = (M, θ, ξ) represent T and put M' := η(M), θ' := θ∘ι, ξ' := ξ∘ι; then θ'(η(y)) = θ(y) and ξ'(η(y)) = ξ(y).
 (a) M' is Borel by step 1, and M' ⊆ η(U) since M ⊆ U.
 (b) M' is countably n-rectifiable: choose M₀ with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) (Simon 3.1.1, SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable). Then Hⁿ(η(M₀)) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·0 = 0 by hausdorff_scaling (i); each η∘F_j is Lipschitz, since η is the linear map λ⁻¹·id (Lipschitz with constant ‖λ⁻¹·id‖) followed by a translation (an isometry); and M' ⊆ η(M₀) ∪ ⋃_j (η∘F_j)(ℝⁿ), because y ∈ M₀ gives η(y) ∈ η(M₀) and y = F_j(v) gives η(y) = (η∘F_j)(v).
 (c) θ' is measurable (θ is measurable and ι is continuous) and ℕ-valued; for z = η(y) ∈ M' with y ∈ M, θ'(z) = θ(y) > 0.
 (d) Local integrability: let K ⊆ η(U) be compact. Then M' ∩ K = η(M ∩ η⁻¹(K)) (f(s ∩ f⁻¹(t)) = f(s) ∩ t for every map f; Set.image_inter_preimage), and M ∩ η⁻¹(K) is Borel (K is closed). The set η⁻¹(K) is compact (η is a homeomorphism) and η⁻¹(K) ⊆ η⁻¹(η(U)) = U, so the last integral is finite by the local integrability of R; as c < ∞ the product is finite.
 (e) ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M' by 2(D), because ξ'∘η = ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M.
 (f) Orientation: let p(z) be the statement “∃Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' z Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ'(z)) Q”. For Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q; for such y the sibling tangent_invariance gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (η(M)) (η(y)) Q, and ξ'(η(y)) = ξ(y), so p(η(y)) holds. Hence p∘η holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e., and by 2(C) p holds Hⁿ⌞M'-a.e.
 Therefore R' := (M', θ', ξ') is an IMRep in η(U).
4. R' represents η_#T. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)). By testform_correspondence (a) choose ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y; by testform_correspondence (c) and since R represents T, η_#T(ω) = λ^{−n}T(ω') = λ^{−n}R.action(ω') = λ^{−n}∫_M θ(y)ξ(y)(ω(η(y))) dHⁿ(y). subproblems.title: Blow-up calculus: mass scaling, pull-back form of currentEval, composition of blow-ups
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0. Write η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(p) = λ⁻¹(p − x). For an n-form ω on ℝ^P let η^#ω := affinePullbackForm (dilationCLM P λ) (−λ⁻¹x) ω, i.e. (η^#ω)(p) = ω(η(p))∘(λ⁻¹·id). Then: (i) for every W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(η_{x,λ#}T) = λ^{−n}·M_{η⁻¹(W)}(T) in [0, ∞], i.e. (blowUp T x λ).massOn W = ofReal(λ⁻¹ⁿ)·T.massOn (dilation x λ ⁻¹' W); (ii) currentEval(η_{x,λ#}T, ω) = currentEval(T, η^#ω) for every n-form ω on ℝ^P; (iii) for every y ∈ ℝ^P, μ > 0 and every n-form ω, currentEval(η_{y,μ#}(η_{x,λ#}T), ω) = currentEval(η_{x+λy,λμ#}T, ω). Here currentEval(A, ω) = A(ω) if ω is a test form with support in the domain of A, and 0 otherwise.

Source: the dilation identities used throughout the parent proof (step 1: "under any dilation μ_{η_{y,λ#}A} = λ^{−n}(η_{y,λ})_#μ_A"; step 2(c),(e): η_{y,λ′}∘η_{x_i,λ_i} = η_{x_i+λ_iy,λ_iλ′} and A_{k,i}(ω) = (η_{x_i,s_i#}T′)(η_{y,λ_k}^#ω)), proved here from the definitions of blowUp (Simon 6.2.23), massOn (6.2.5) and currentEval. Part (i) is proved directly in step 5 by the correspondence of admissible forms. (The same identity in image form, (blowUp T x λ).massOn (dilation x λ '' W) = ofReal(λ⁻¹ⁿ)·T.massOn W, is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image of node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.blowup_scaling-a1.mass_scaling-a1. It is a reading reference only, not a dependency of this child; the numbered proof is self-contained.)
1. (Facts about η and η^#.) η is an affine bijection of ℝ^P with inverse η⁻¹(q) = x + λq; both maps are homeomorphisms, and η⁻¹(B_ρ(w)) = B_{λρ}(x + λw). For an n-form ω and a point p, multilinearity gives (η^#ω)(p)(v_1, …, v_n) = ω(η p)(λ⁻¹v_1, …, λ⁻¹v_n) = λ^{−n}·ω(η p)(v_1, …, v_n), i.e. (η^#ω)(p) = λ^{−n}ω(η(p)). Consequently:
(a) (η^#ω)(p) = 0 iff ω(η(p)) = 0. So support(η^#ω) = η⁻¹(support ω), and since η is a homeomorphism, tsupport(η^#ω) = η⁻¹(tsupport ω).
(b) Write (η⁻¹)^#β for the pull-back by η⁻¹, (η⁻¹)^#β(q) = β(x + λq)∘(λ·id), which is affinePullbackForm (λ·id) x β. Pull-back is contravariant: affinePullbackForm L₁ b₁ (affinePullbackForm L₂ b₂ ω) = affinePullbackForm (L₂∘L₁) (b₂ + L₂b₁) ω, by evaluating both sides at p. In particular η^#((η⁻¹)^#β) = β and (η⁻¹)^#(η^#ω) = ω.
(c) Affine pull-backs preserve C^∞ forms (affinePullbackForm_isSmoothForm), and η and η⁻¹ are proper. By (a) and (b), IsTestForm(η^#ω) ↔ IsTestForm(ω).
(d) covectorEuclideanNorm((η^#ω)(p)) = λ^{−n}·covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(η(p))), because all coordinate coefficients of the covector are multiplied by λ^{−n}.
2. (Unfolding blowUp.) By definition, blowUp T x λ = (T.restrictDomain h).affinePushforward (dilationCLM P λ) (−λ⁻¹x) hproper, where the restricted domain η⁻¹(η(U)) equals U. Hence for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) (TestFormOn (dilation x λ '' U) n), (blowUp T x λ)(ω) = T(η^#ω). Here η^#ω is regarded as an element of TestFormOn U n, since tsupport η^#ω = η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(η(U)) = U (affinePushforward_apply, restrictDomain_apply, testFormOnInclusion_coe; currents applied to equal underlying forms agree by proof irrelevance).
3. (Proof of (ii).) Suppose ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ η(U). By 1(a),(c), η^#ω is a test form with tsupport ⊆ U, so by step 2 and the definition of currentEval both sides equal T(η^#ω). Otherwise, either ω is not a test form, and then neither is η^#ω (1(c)); or tsupport ω ⊄ η(U), and then tsupport η^#ω = η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊄ U (η is bijective). In both cases both sides are 0.
4. (Proof of (iii).) Let η₁ := dilation x λ, η₂ := dilation y μ and η₃ := dilation (x + λy) (λμ). Then η₂∘η₁ = η₃, since μ⁻¹(λ⁻¹(p − x) − y) = (λμ)⁻¹(p − x − λy). By the composition rule 1(b), η₁^#(η₂^#ω) = η₃^#ω as forms: the linear parts are μ⁻¹λ⁻¹·id = (λμ)⁻¹·id and the translations agree by the displayed identity. Applying (ii) twice gives
currentEval(blowUp (blowUp T x λ) y μ, ω) = currentEval(blowUp T x λ, η₂^#ω) = currentEval(T, η₁^#η₂^#ω) = currentEval(T, η₃^#ω) = currentEval(blowUp T (x + λy) (λμ), ω).
5. (Proof of (i).) Let W ⊆ ℝ^P and write W′ := η⁻¹(W) = dilation x λ ⁻¹' W. By definition (SimonGMT massOn), M_W(blowUp T x λ) is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal((blowUp T x λ)(ω)) over the admissible set 𝒜 := massAdmissibleOn (η(U)) n W = {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) : tsupport ω ⊆ W, covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(q)) ≤ 1 for all q}, and M_{W′}(T) is the supremum of ofReal(T(β)) over ℬ := massAdmissibleOn U n W′ = {β ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) : tsupport β ⊆ W′, covectorEuclideanNorm(β(p)) ≤ 1 for all p}.
(a) Φ(ω) := λⁿ·η^#ω maps 𝒜 into ℬ. By 1(a), 1(c) and step 2, η^#ω is a test form with tsupport η^#ω = η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(W) ∩ η⁻¹(η(U)) = W′ ∩ U, so Φ(ω) ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and tsupport Φ(ω) ⊆ W′. By 1(d), covectorEuclideanNorm(Φ(ω)(p)) = λⁿ·λ^{−n}·covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(η(p))) ≤ 1.
(b) Ψ(β) := λ^{−n}·(η⁻¹)^#β maps ℬ into 𝒜. The map η⁻¹(q) = x + λq is a proper affine bijection with linear part λ·id, so (η⁻¹)^#β(q) = β(x + λq)∘(λ·id) = λⁿβ(η⁻¹(q)) is smooth, tsupport (η⁻¹)^#β = η(tsupport β) is compact and contained in η(W′) ∩ η(U) ⊆ W ∩ η(U), and covectorEuclideanNorm(Ψ(β)(q)) = λ^{−n}·λⁿ·covectorEuclideanNorm(β(η⁻¹(q))) ≤ 1 (the computation of 1(d) with λ replaced by λ⁻¹).
(c) By 1(b), η^#((η⁻¹)^#β) = β and (η⁻¹)^#(η^#ω) = ω, so Φ(Ψ(β)) = β and Ψ(Φ(ω)) = ω: Φ is a bijection 𝒜 → ℬ.
(d) For ω ∈ 𝒜, step 2 and linearity give (blowUp T x λ)(ω) = T(η^#ω) = λ^{−n}·T(Φ(ω)). Hence, by (c), {ofReal((blowUp T x λ)(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒜} = {ofReal(λ^{−n}·T(β)) : β ∈ ℬ} = {ofReal(λ^{−n})·ofReal(T(β)) : β ∈ ℬ}, using ofReal(ab) = ofReal(a)·ofReal(b) for a ≥ 0.
(e) Taking suprema, and using that multiplication by the finite constant ofReal(λ^{−n}) commutes with suprema in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.mul_sSup, or ENNReal.mul_iSup), M_W(blowUp T x λ) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·M_{W′}(T). Since λ^{−n} = (λ⁻¹)ⁿ, this is (blowUp T x λ).massOn W = ofReal(λ⁻¹ⁿ)·T.massOn (dilation x λ ⁻¹' W), which is (i). It holds for every W ⊆ ℝ^P, open or not, and for every U.
6. Parts (i), (ii) and (iii) are proved in steps 5, 3 and 4. ∎
proof_key_steps: η^#ω(p) = λ^{−n}ω(η(p)); hence tsupport η^#ω = η⁻¹(tsupport ω), test forms correspond, the coefficient norm scales by λ^{−n}, and affine pull-backs compose contravariantly.
Unfolding blowUp (restrictDomain + affinePushforward) gives (η_{x,λ#}T)(ω) = T(η^#ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)); case analysis on the currentEval guard proves (ii).
(iii) follows from (ii) applied twice and η_{y,μ}∘η_{x,λ} = η_{x+λy,λμ}.

Source: parent proof, step 2(e), case λ = 0, "Diagonal selection" (with the uniform bounds of step 2(d) and criterion (C)), stated directly for blow-ups of T. Uses the sibling lemma blowup_calculus (Submission.dimred_tr_blowup_calculus: (i) mass scaling, (ii) currentEval(η_{a,t#}A, ω) = currentEval(A, η_{a,t}^#ω), (iii) composition). The countable-test criterion (C) of parent step 2(d) is proved in Step A below as Lemma CT.

Step A (Lemma CT; formerly the separate sibling countable_tests of attempt 4, merged here because this child is its only user). Within this step the letters below denote the objects of Lemma CT only.
Lemma CT (criterion (C) of parent step 2(d)). Let P, n ∈ ℕ. There is a sequence (ω_m) in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) with the following property. Let V_k ⊆ ℝ^P (k ∈ ℕ) be sets, A_k ∈ 𝒟_n(V_k) and A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Suppose that for every R ∈ ℕ there are k₀ ∈ ℕ and Γ ∈ [0, ∞) with M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(A) ≤ Γ and, for all k ≥ k₀, B_{R+1}(0) ⊆ V_k and M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(A_k) ≤ Γ. Suppose also that currentEval(A_k, ω_m) → A(ω_m) as k → ∞ for every m. Then A_k ⇀ A in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly), i.e. currentEval(A_k, ω) → A(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P).
Proof of Lemma CT.
Source: parent proof, step 2(d), "Countable-test criterion for limits on ℝ^P approximated by currents whose domains exhaust ℝ^P" (criterion (C)). The parent builds the countable family from polynomials (Weierstrass). Stone–Weierstrass and the separability of C(X, Y) are not reachable from the frozen header (checked: polynomialFunctions_closure_eq_top and ContinuousMap.instSeparableSpace are unknown after import GMT.Ch07.Submission). The family is therefore built below from an explicit smooth partition of unity on a grid, with the same property (★). Steps CT2 and CT3 are the parent's argument. |·| denotes covectorEuclideanNorm, the coefficient norm in Simon's mass: |α| = (Σ_I α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2} over strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P. It is the Euclidean norm of a linear image of α, hence a seminorm: |α + β| ≤ |α| + |β| and |cα| = |c||α|.

CT1. (A countable approximating family.) We construct a countable family {ω_m} ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) = TestFormOn univ n with property (★): for every R ∈ ℕ, every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0) and every ε > 0, there is m with tsupport ω_m ⊆ B_{R+1}(0) and |ω(p) − ω_m(p)| < ε for all p ∈ ℝ^P.
(a) A partition of unity on ℝ. Let s := Real.smoothTransition: C^∞, monotone, s(u) = 0 for u ≤ 0, s(u) = 1 for u ≥ 1. Put β(u) := s(u + 1) − s(u). Then β is C^∞ and β ≥ 0 (monotone), and β(u) = 0 unless −1 < u < 1: for u ≥ 1 both terms are 1, for u ≤ −1 both are 0. For every u ∈ ℝ, Σ_{j∈ℤ} β(u − j) = 1. Indeed, let j₀ := ⌊u⌋. Only j ∈ {j₀ − 1, j₀, j₀ + 1} (in fact only j₀ and j₀ + 1) can contribute, and the three terms telescope to s(u − j₀ + 2) − s(u − j₀ − 1) = 1 − 0, because u − j₀ + 2 ≥ 2 and u − j₀ − 1 < 0.
(b) A partition of unity on ℝ^P. For δ > 0 and g ∈ ℤ^P put ψ^δ_g(x) := ∏_{i<P} β(x_i/δ − g_i), where x_i is the i-th coordinate of x ∈ Euclid P. Then:
 - ψ^δ_g is C^∞, as a finite product of C^∞ functions of continuous linear coordinates;
 - 0 ≤ ψ^δ_g;
 - if ψ^δ_g(x) ≠ 0, then |x_i − δg_i| < δ for every i, hence |x − δg| ≤ δ√P (with equality only if P = 0). So tsupport ψ^δ_g ⊆ B̄_{δ√P}(δg) and ψ^δ_g has compact support;
 - for every x, Σ_{g∈ℤ^P} ψ^δ_g(x) = ∏_{i<P} Σ_{j∈ℤ} β(x_i/δ − j) = 1, with only finitely many nonzero terms.
(c) Dense covectors. Covector (Euclid P) n = (Euclid P) [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ is a normed space. It is finite-dimensional: α ↦ (α(e_{J(1)}, …, e_{J(n)}))_{J : Fin n → Fin P} is a linear map into the finite-dimensional space (Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ, and it is injective, because an alternating map is determined by its values on tuples of basis vectors (Module.Basis.ext_alternating, applied to the underlying alternating map). No FiniteDimensional or SeparableSpace instance for Covector is inferred after import GMT.Ch07.Submission; the local instance obtained here (FiniteDimensional.of_injective) makes SeparableSpace inferable. So it is proper and second countable, hence separable. Fix a sequence (α_l)_{l∈ℕ} dense for the operator norm ‖·‖. Each coefficient satisfies |α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖e_{I(i)}‖ = ‖α‖, so |α| ≤ √(Pⁿ)·‖α‖. Hence (α_l) is also dense for |·|.
(d) The family. For j ∈ ℕ put δ_j := 1/((j + 1)(P + 1)), so δ_j√P < 1. Take all forms
 ω_{j,G,a}(x) := Σ_{g∈G} ψ^{δ_j}_g(x) • α_{a(g)},
 with j ∈ ℕ, G ⊆ ℤ^P finite and a : G → ℕ. These index triples form a countable set. Each ω_{j,G,a} is a C^∞ map ℝ^P → Covector: a finite sum of C^∞ scalar functions times constant covectors. It has compact support (tsupport ⊆ ⋃_{g∈G} tsupport ψ^{δ_j}_g, a finite union of compact sets), so it is a test form in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ⊆ univ. The empty G gives the zero form, so the family is nonempty. Enumerate it surjectively as (ω_m)_{m∈ℕ}, by a surjection from ℕ onto a countable nonempty set.
(e) Proof of (★).
 - Let R, ω and ε be given. ω is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous. Since |α| ≤ √(Pⁿ)·‖α‖ by (c), the seminorm |·| is Lipschitz for the operator norm. So there is δ₀ > 0 with |ω(x) − ω(y)| < ε/3 whenever |x − y| < δ₀.
 - Choose j with δ_j√P < δ₀ and put δ := δ_j. Let G := {g ∈ ℤ^P : |δg| < R}, which is finite. For g ∈ G choose a(g) with |ω(δg) − α_{a(g)}| < ε/3, by (c). Put ω′ := ω_{j,G,a}.
 - Support. tsupport ω′ ⊆ ⋃_{g∈G} B̄_{δ√P}(δg) ⊆ B̄_{R+δ√P}(0) ⊆ B_{R+1}(0), since |δg| < R and δ√P < 1.
 - Estimate. If g ∉ G, then |δg| ≥ R, so δg ∉ B_R(0) ⊇ tsupport ω and ω(δg) = 0. Using Σ_g ψ^δ_g(x) = 1, for every x:
 ω(x) − ω′(x) = Σ_{g∈ℤ^P} ψ^δ_g(x)·(ω(x) − ω(δg)) + Σ_{g∈G} ψ^δ_g(x)·(ω(δg) − α_{a(g)}),
 a finite sum, because only finitely many ψ^δ_g(x) ≠ 0. If ψ^δ_g(x) ≠ 0 then |x − δg| ≤ δ√P < δ₀, so |ω(x) − ω(δg)| < ε/3. By the seminorm property and ψ^δ_g ≥ 0, Σ_g ψ^δ_g(x) = 1,
 |ω(x) − ω′(x)| ≤ Σ_g ψ^δ_g(x)·ε/3 + Σ_g ψ^δ_g(x)·ε/3 ≤ 2ε/3 < ε.
 - So ω′ = ω_m for some m, and it has the properties required in (★).

CT2. (Mass controls test values.) Let A′ ∈ 𝒟_n(V′), O ⊆ ℝ^P and β ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V′) with tsupport β ⊆ O and |β(p)| ≤ s for all p. Suppose M_O(A′) < ∞. Then |A′(β)| ≤ s·M_O(A′).toReal.
- If s > 0, then ±β/s belong to massAdmissibleOn V′ n O, so ofReal(±A′(β)/s) ≤ M_O(A′) by GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn.
- If s = 0, then β = 0. Indeed |β(p)| = 0 forces every strictly increasing coefficient of β(p) to vanish. An alternating map that vanishes on all strictly increasing basis tuples is zero: permuting a tuple changes the value by a sign, and a tuple with a repeated basis vector gives 0.

CT3. (Proof of the criterion.)
- Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Choose R ∈ ℕ with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0), which exists by compact support. Take k₀ and Γ from the hypothesis for this R.
- Let ε > 0 and choose m by (★). For k ≥ k₀, tsupport ω and tsupport ω_m lie in B_{R+1}(0) ⊆ V_k. So currentEval(A_k, ω) = A_k(ω) and currentEval(A_k, ω_m) = A_k(ω_m).
- β := ω − ω_m has tsupport ⊆ B_{R+1}(0) and |β| ≤ ε. By linearity and step CT2 with O = B_{R+1}(0) and s = ε, |currentEval(A_k, ω) − currentEval(A_k, ω_m)| ≤ εΓ. Likewise |A(ω) − A(ω_m)| ≤ εΓ.
- Since currentEval(A_k, ω_m) → A(ω_m), limsup_k |currentEval(A_k, ω) − A(ω)| ≤ 2εΓ.
- As ε > 0 is arbitrary and Γ does not depend on ε, currentEval(A_k, ω) → A(ω).
This holds for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), which is ConvergesWeakly (A_k) A. ∎

Main argument.
Notation: B_i := blowUp T x_i λ_i ∈ 𝒟_n(η_{x_i,λ_i}(U)); A_{k,i} := blowUp T (x_i + λ_iy) (λ_is_k); η_k^#ω := affinePullbackForm (dilationCLM P s_k) (−s_k⁻¹y) ω. Note η_{y,s_k}(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P, so blowUp S y s_k and S are currents on (sets equal to) ℝ^P.
0. (Normalization of Γ.) Hypothesis (a) stays true when Γ is replaced by max(Γ, 0), since ofReal is monotone. So assume Γ ≥ 0; then all the real bounds Γρⁿ below are nonnegative and ofReal(Γρⁿ) = Γρⁿ.
1. (Exhausting domains.) Choose δ′ > 0 with B_{2δ′}(x) ⊆ U (U open, x ∈ U). If x″ ∈ B_{δ′}(x) and t > 0, then dilation x″ t '' U ⊇ dilation x″ t '' B_{δ′}(x″) = B_{δ′/t}(0). Consequently, if x″_k → x and t_k → 0, every compact subset of ℝ^P lies in the domain of blowUp T x″_k t_k for all large k. This applies to (x_i, λ_i).
2. (Mass bounds for blow-ups of T.) By blowup_calculus (i) and dilation a t ⁻¹' B_ρ(p) = B_{tρ}(a + tp): M_{B_ρ(p)}(blowUp T a t) = t^{−n}M_{B_{tρ}(a+tp)}(T) ≤ t^{−n}Γ(tρ)ⁿ = Γρⁿ (as elements of [0, ∞], via ofReal) whenever a + tp ∈ B_δ(x) and tρ < δ.
3. (Mass bounds for S.) Let p ∈ ℝ^P, ρ > 0 and β ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) admissible for M_{B_ρ(p)}(S), i.e. tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ(p) and |β| ≤ 1. For large i, tsupport β lies in the domain of B_i (step 1). Then β is admissible for M_{B_ρ(p)}(B_i), and currentEval(B_i, β) = B_i(β) ≤ M_{B_ρ(p)}(B_i).toReal ≤ Γρⁿ (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn and step 2, as x_i + λ_ip → x and λ_iρ → 0). By (b), S(β) = lim_i currentEval(B_i, β) ≤ Γρⁿ. Taking the supremum, M_{B_ρ(p)}(S) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for all p ∈ ℝ^P and ρ > 0.
4. (Mass bounds for η_{y,s_k#}S and for C.) By blowup_calculus (i), M_{B_ρ(0)}(blowUp S y s_k) = s_k^{−n}M_{B_{s_kρ}(y)}(S) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) by step 3. If β is admissible for M_{B_ρ(0)}(C), then C(β) = lim_k currentEval(blowUp S y s_k, β) by (c). Each term equals (blowUp S y s_k)(β) ≤ Γρⁿ, since the domain is all of ℝ^P. Hence M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ).
5. (Inner convergence for fixed k.) Fix k and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). By blowup_calculus (iii), applied to B_i with centre y and scale s_k (note (x_i + λ_iy, λ_is_k) are the composed parameters), and then (ii):
currentEval(A_{k,i}, ω) = currentEval(blowUp B_i y s_k, ω) = currentEval(B_i, η_k^#ω).
η_k^#ω is a test form on ℝ^P (affine pull-backs by proper affine maps preserve test forms). So by (b), currentEval(B_i, η_k^#ω) → S(η_k^#ω) as i → ∞. Moreover S(η_k^#ω) = currentEval(S, η_k^#ω) = currentEval(blowUp S y s_k, ω) by (ii) for S. Hence currentEval(A_{k,i}, ω) → currentEval(blowUp S y s_k, ω) as i → ∞.
6. (Diagonal selection.) Let (ω_m) be the family given by Lemma CT (Step A) for (P, n). Choose inductively i(0) < i(1) < … such that for each k: i(k) > i(k − 1); λ_{i(k)} < 1/(k+1); |x_{i(k)} − x| < 1/(k+1); and |currentEval(A_{k,i(k)}, ω_m) − currentEval(blowUp S y s_k, ω_m)| < 1/(k+1) for all m ≤ k. These are finitely many conditions, each true for all large i by step 5, λ_i → 0 and x_i → x. Put φ(k) := i(k), x′_k := x_{φ(k)} + λ_{φ(k)}y, λ′_k := λ_{φ(k)}s_k and D_k := A_{k,φ(k)} = blowUp T x′_k λ′_k. Then φ is strictly increasing, x′_k → x and λ′_k → 0.

(a) Domains and masses. Given R ∈ ℕ, choose k₀ such that for k ≥ k₀: x′_k ∈ B_{min(δ,δ′)}(x), λ′_k(R + 1) < δ, and R + 1 < δ′/λ′_k. Then B_{R+1}(0) ⊆ dom D_k (step 1) and M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(D_k) ≤ ofReal(Γ(R+1)ⁿ) (step 2 with p = 0). Also M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(C) ≤ ofReal(Γ(R+1)ⁿ) (step 4). Take Γ_R := ofReal(Γ(R+1)ⁿ) < ∞.
(b) Tests. For each m and k ≥ m: |currentEval(D_k, ω_m) − C(ω_m)| < 1/(k+1) + |currentEval(blowUp S y s_k, ω_m) − C(ω_m)|, and the last term → 0 by (c). So currentEval(D_k, ω_m) → C(ω_m).
By Lemma CT (Step A), D_k ⇀ C in ℝ^P, i.e. ConvergesWeakly (fun k ↦ blowUp T (x_{φ(k)} + λ_{φ(k)}•y) (λ_{φ(k)}·s_k)) C. ∎

That is: for all P′, n′, Q′ ∈ ℕ, every set F of functions ℝ^{P′} → ℝ^{Q′} and every map sing satisfying (H0), local μH[n′]-integrability, A.1, A.2 and A.3 (closedness, emptiness for flat indicators of n′-planes, rescaling, and the ε-neighbourhood semicontinuity), either (I) B_1(0) ∩ sing φ = ∅ for all φ ∈ F, or (II) there is d with d + 1 ≤ n′ such that μH[d + α](sing φ ∩ B_1(0)) = 0 for all φ ∈ F and α > 0, some ψ ∈ F and a d-dimensional subspace L have sing ψ = L and ψ(y + λx) = ψ(x) for y ∈ L and λ > 0, and, if d = 0, sing φ ∩ B_σ(0) is finite for all φ ∈ F and σ < 1. Under (ADR): Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, c > 0, Λ ∈ ℝ, and let 𝓜 be a set of Borel measures on ℝ^P. For a measure μ and x ∈ ℝ^P let dens μ x := (limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ)).toReal (limsup in [0, ∞], ω_n = unitBallVolume n; toReal sends ∞ to 0). For y ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 put μ^{y,λ} := ofReal(λ⁻¹ⁿ) • μ.map (dilation y λ) (= λ^{−n}(η_{y,λ})_#μ). Then either (I) for every μ ∈ 𝓜 the set {x ∈ B_1(0) : c ≤ dens μ x} is empty; or (II) there is d ∈ ℕ with d + 1 ≤ n such that μH[d + α]({x ∈ B_1(0) : c ≤ dens μ x}) = 0 for all μ ∈ 𝓜 and real α > 0; if d = 0, {x ∈ B_σ(0) : c ≤ dens μ x} is finite for all μ ∈ 𝓜 and σ < 1; and there are ν ∈ 𝓜 with ν(ℝ^P) = ∞ and a linear subspace L with dim L = d, {x : c ≤ dens ν x} = L and dens ν (y + λx) = dens ν x for all y ∈ L, λ > 0 and x. (In the Lean statement dens is a universally quantified function fixed by its defining equation.)

Lemma D (parent step 4, for measures). Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Λ ∈ ℝ, and let μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) and μ be Borel measures on ℝ^P, each finite on compact sets, with ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Assume that for every j, every y ∈ ℝ^P and every R with B̄_R(y) ⊆ B̄_2(0), the function ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·μ_j(B_ρ(y)) is nondecreasing on (0, R). Let w_j → w in ℝ^P with |w| < 2, and let θ_j, θ, c ∈ ℝ with θ ≥ 0, μ_j(B_ρ(w_j))/(ω_nρⁿ) → ofReal(θ_j) and μ(B_ρ(w))/(ω_nρⁿ) → ofReal(θ) as ρ ↓ 0 (ω_n = unitBallVolume n, in [0, ∞]), and c ≤ θ_j for every j. Then c ≤ θ.
Proof of Lemma D.
Source: parent proof, step 4 ("Semicontinuity along members"): Θ_S(w) ≥ limsup_k Θ_{S_k}(w_k), via the monotonicity bound at w_k, inclusion of balls, upper semicontinuity of vague limits on compact sets, then η ↓ 0 and ρ ↓ 0. It is stated here for measures, with only what the argument uses.

As ρ ↓ 0, ofReal(e^{Λρ}) → 1, so g_j(ρ) → ω_n·ofReal(θ_j). Since g_j is nondecreasing on (0, R₀/2), for every ρ in that interval ω_n·ofReal(θ_j) = lim_{t↓0} g_j(t) ≤ g_j(ρ). As ofReal(c) ≤ ofReal(θ_j), we get μ_j(B_ρ(w_j)) ≥ ofReal(c)·ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}) for all j ≥ j₁ and ρ ∈ (0, R₀/2).
D3. (Passing to μ.) Fix ρ ∈ (0, R₀/2) and η > 0. For large j, |w_j − w| ≤ η, so B_ρ(w_j) ⊆ K := B̄_{ρ+η}(w), which is compact.
Claim: limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K). For ε > 0 let K_ε := {p : dist(p, K) ≤ ε} (compact) and f_ε(p) := max(0, 1 − dist(p, K)/ε). Then f_ε is continuous with compact support and 1_K ≤ f_ε ≤ 1_{K_ε}. Since μ_j is finite on compact sets, f_ε is μ_j-integrable and μ_j(K) ≤ ∫ f_ε dμ_j → ∫ f_ε dμ ≤ μ(K_ε). Finally μ(K_ε) ↓ μ(K) as ε ↓ 0, because K = ⋂_ε K_ε and μ(K_1) < ∞.
By the claim and step D2, μ(B̄_{ρ+η}(w)) ≥ ofReal(c)·ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}) for every η > 0. Letting η ↓ 0 (μ is finite on B̄_{ρ+1}(w) and B̄_ρ(w) = ⋂_η B̄_{ρ+η}(w)) gives μ(B̄_ρ(w)) ≥ ofReal(c)·ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿe^{−Λρ}).
D4. (Back to open balls.) For t ∈ (0, R₀/2) and ε > 0 put ρ := t/(1 + ε) < t. Then μ(B_t(w)) ≥ μ(B̄_ρ(w)) ≥ ofReal(c)·ω_n·ofReal(tⁿ(1 + ε)^{−n}e^{−Λρ}). Since |Λρ| ≤ |Λ|t, this gives μ(B_t(w))/(ω_ntⁿ) ≥ ofReal(c)·ofReal((1 + ε)^{−n}e^{−|Λ|t}). If c ≤ 0 the bound is trivial. Letting t ↓ 0 gives ofReal(θ) ≥ ofReal(c)·ofReal((1 + ε)^{−n}), and letting ε ↓ 0 gives ofReal(θ) ≥ ofReal(c).

Main argument.
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]. c_n := addHaarScalarFactor(volume, μH[n]) ∈ ℝ≥0, with Hⁿ = c_n·μH[n] (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def) and c_n ≠ 0 (addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero). So μH[n] and Hⁿ have the same null sets, and ∫ g dμH[n] = c_n⁻¹∫ g dHⁿ. q(μ, x, ρ) := μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) ∈ [0, ∞], so dens μ x = (limsup_{ρ↓0} q(μ, x, ρ)).toReal ≥ 0. e := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ Euclid 1, so ⟨v, e⟩ = v 0 and e 0 = 1. φ_μ(x) := dens μ x • e. F := {φ_μ : μ ∈ 𝓜}. For φ : ℝ^P → Euclid 1, sing φ := closure{x : c ≤ φ(x) 0}. Note c ≤ φ_μ(x) 0 iff c ≤ dens μ x.
1. (Measurability; parent 3(ii).) Let μ be any Borel measure. For fixed ρ > 0, x ↦ μ(B_ρ(x)) is lower semicontinuous: if x_j → x then B_ρ(x) ⊆ ⋃_m ⋂_{j≥m} B_ρ(x_j), so μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ liminf_j μ(B_ρ(x_j)) by continuity from below. Equivalently, in filter form: if y < μ(B_ρ(x)), pick r < ρ with y < μ(B_r(x)); then B_r(x) ⊆ B_ρ(x′) whenever |x′ − x| < ρ − r. For fixed x, ρ ↦ q(μ, x, ρ) is left-continuous on (0, ∞): B_ρ(x) = ⋃_{ρ′<ρ} B_{ρ′}(x), and ρⁿ is continuous and positive. Hence limsup_{ρ↓0} q(μ, x, ρ) = inf_{δ ∈ ℚ_{>0}} sup_{ρ ∈ ℚ∩(0,δ)} q(μ, x, ρ), a countable infimum of countable suprema of Borel functions of x. So dens μ is Borel. Here "left-continuous" is used through the following elementary fact, proved the same way as for right-continuity: if g : (0, δ) → [0, ∞] is left-continuous at every ρ ∈ (0, δ), then sup_{(0,δ)} g = sup_{ℚ∩(0,δ)} g, because each ρ ∈ (0, δ) is the limit of rationals q_m ↑ ρ with q_m ∈ (0, ρ), so g(ρ) = lim g(q_m) ≤ sup_{ℚ∩(0,δ)} g. Lower semicontinuous functions are Borel (LowerSemicontinuous.measurable), and countable infima and suprema of measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions are measurable; toReal is measurable. (Both facts are proved directly here. SimonGMT's Chapter01/Densities.lean is not imported by the frozen header, and its lemma iSup_rat_Ioo_eq_of_tendsto_right assumes right-continuity in the radius, which fails for open balls, e.g. for a Dirac mass at distance 1 from x.)
2. (Rescaling identity; parent 3(vi).) For any measure μ, y ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, dilation y λ ⁻¹' B_ρ(x) = B_{λρ}(y + λx). So μ^{y,λ}(B_ρ(x)) = ofReal(λ^{−n})μ(B_{λρ}(y + λx)) and q(μ^{y,λ}, x, ρ) = q(μ, y + λx, λρ). The map ρ ↦ λρ sends 𝓝[>]0 onto 𝓝[>]0 (Filter.map of 𝓝[>]0 under multiplication by λ > 0 is 𝓝[>]0, a small lemma), so the limsups coincide: dens μ^{y,λ} x = dens μ (y + λx), i.e. φ_{μ^{y,λ}} = φ_μ(y + λ·).
3. (Homogeneity; parent 3(vii).) If ν(λ·s) = λⁿν(s) for all λ > 0 and Borel s, then ν(B_ρ(λx)) = ν(λ·B_{ρ/λ}(x)) = λⁿν(B_{ρ/λ}(x)). So q(ν, λx, ρ) = q(ν, x, ρ/λ), and dens ν (λx) = dens ν x.
4. (Normalized pairings; parent 3(iv),(v).) Let μ ∈ 𝓜 and f be continuous with compact support. By (2), μ = Hⁿ.withDensity(ofReal∘dens μ) = (c_n • μH[n]).withDensity(ofReal∘dens μ), with dens μ Borel (step 1) and finite, and c_n ∈ ℝ≥0. By integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul over the measure c_n • μH[n], then integral_smul_nnreal_measure, ∫ f dμ = c_n∫ dens μ·f dμH[n]. This route compiles; withDensity_smul_measure would need an ℝ≥0∞ scalar. Therefore ∫ f(x)•φ_μ(x) dμH[n](x) = (∫ f·dens μ dμH[n])•e = c_n⁻¹(∫ f dμ)•e. This identity needs no integrability hypothesis: it holds for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul, integral_smul_nnreal_measure and integral_smul_const are unconditional, non-integrable integrands having Bochner integral 0 on both sides), so the uses in (A.2) and (A.3)(3) below carry no side conditions. Likewise ∫_K dens μ dμH[n] = c_n⁻¹μ(K) < ∞ for compact K, by (1).
5. (Densities exist on B_2(0).) Let μ ∈ 𝓜 and |x| < 2, and put R := 2 − |x|, so B̄_R(x) ⊆ B̄_2(0). By (5), g(ρ) := ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)μ(B_ρ(x)) is nondecreasing on (0, R), and it is finite by (1). Hence g(ρ) → L := inf_{(0,R)} g < ∞ as ρ ↓ 0 (MonotoneOn.tendsto_nhdsWithin_Ioo_right), and q(μ, x, ρ) = ofReal(e^{−Λρ})·g(ρ)/ω_n → L/ω_n. So the limsup is a finite limit, and q(μ, x, ρ) → ofReal(dens μ x).
6. (Upper semicontinuity on B_2(0); parent 5(γ).) Let μ ∈ 𝓜, x ∈ B_2(0), and x_j → x with c ≤ dens μ x_j for all j; passing to a tail, x_j ∈ B_2(0). Apply Lemma D (Step 0) with μ_j := μ (constant sequence, so vague convergence is trivial), w_j := x_j, w := x, θ_j := dens μ x_j, θ := dens μ x ≥ 0. Its hypotheses hold by (1), (5) and step 5. So c ≤ dens μ x. Consequently, for μ ∈ 𝓜, sing φ_μ ∩ B_2(0) ⊆ {x : c ≤ dens μ x}, since a point of the closure lying in the open set B_2(0) is a limit of such x_j.
7. (Hypotheses of (ADR) for (P, n, Q := 1, F, sing).)
(H0) Let μ, ν ∈ 𝓜 with φ_μ = φ_ν μH[n]-a.e. Taking coordinate 0, dens μ = dens ν μH[n]-a.e., hence Hⁿ-a.e. By (2) and withDensity_congr_ae, μ = Hⁿ.withDensity(ofReal∘dens μ) = Hⁿ.withDensity(ofReal∘dens ν) = ν. Hence dens μ = dens ν everywhere and φ_μ = φ_ν.
(Loc), the second hypothesis of (ADR), local integrability; not the parent's (H1). φ_μ is Borel (step 1) and ∫_K ‖φ_μ‖ dμH[n] = ∫_K dens μ dμH[n] < ∞ for compact K (step 4, ‖e‖ = 1). So φ_μ is locally μH[n]-integrable (each point has the compact neighbourhood B̄_1(x)).
(A.1) For μ ∈ 𝓜, 0 < λ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ, the function x ↦ φ_μ(y + λx) equals φ_{μ^{y,λ}} (step 2), and μ^{y,λ} ∈ 𝓜 by (3).
(A.2) Let μ ∈ 𝓜, |y| < 1, and λ_k > 0 strictly decreasing to 0. Hypothesis (4) gives sub and a homogeneous ν ∈ 𝓜 with ∫ f dμ^{y,λ_{sub(j)}} → ∫ f dν for all continuous compactly supported f. Put ψ := φ_ν ∈ F; then ψ(λx) = ψ(x) by step 3. For j large, λ_{sub(j)} < 1 − |y| ≤ 1, so μ^{y,λ_{sub(j)}} ∈ 𝓜 by (3). By steps 2 and 4, ∫ f(x)•φ_μ(y + λ_{sub(j)}x) dμH[n] = ∫ f•φ_{μ^{y,λ_{sub(j)}}} dμH[n] = c_n⁻¹(∫ f dμ^{y,λ_{sub(j)}})•e → c_n⁻¹(∫ f dν)•e = ∫ f•ψ dμH[n].
(A.3) Closedness: sing φ is a closure.
(A.3)(1) Let μ ∈ 𝓜, L an n-dimensional subspace and c″ ∈ Euclid 1 with φ_μ = 1_L·c″. Put c′ := c″ 0. Comparing coordinate 0, dens μ x = c′ for x ∈ L and = 0 for x ∉ L.
– If c′ < c, then {x : c ≤ dens μ x} = ∅ (on L the value is c′ < c, off L it is 0 < c), so sing φ_μ = closure ∅ = ∅.
– If c′ ≥ c, then by (2), μ = Hⁿ.withDensity(ofReal(c′)·1_L) and μ(ℝ^P) = ofReal(c′)·Hⁿ(L) = ∞. Here c′ ≥ c > 0, and Hⁿ(L) = ∞ because L with the induced inner product is isometric to ℝⁿ, Hⁿ restricted to L is its volume (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), and volume(ℝⁿ) = ∞ for n ≥ 1 (MeasureTheory.measure_univ_of_isAddLeftInvariant: ℝⁿ is not compact for n ≥ 1). Hypothesis (6) is contradicted.
So sing φ_μ = ∅ in all cases.
(A.3)(2) For λ > 0, w ↦ y + λw is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P. Hence sing(φ(y + λ·)) = closure((y + λ·)⁻¹{c ≤ φ(·) 0}) = (y + λ·)⁻¹(closure{c ≤ φ(·) 0}) = (y + λ·)⁻¹(sing φ) for every φ.
(A.3)(3) (parent 5(ε).) Let μ ∈ 𝓜 and φ_k ∈ F with ∫ f•φ_k dμH[n] → ∫ f•φ_μ dμH[n] for all continuous compactly supported f, and let ε > 0. Choose μ_k ∈ 𝓜 with φ_k = φ_{μ_k}. By step 4 (apply ⟨·, e⟩ and multiply by c_n), ∫ f dμ_k → ∫ f dμ. Suppose the conclusion fails. Then there are k_1 < k_2 < … and w_j ∈ B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_{μ_{k_j}} with dist(w_j, z) ≥ ε for all z ∈ sing φ_μ. By step 6, c ≤ dens μ_{k_j} w_j. After passing to a further subsequence, w_j → w with |w| ≤ 1 < 2. Apply Lemma D (Step 0) to the measures μ_{k_j} and μ: (1) and (5) hold, vague convergence holds along the subsequence, the densities at w_j and at w exist by step 5, and θ := dens μ w ≥ 0. It gives c ≤ dens μ w, so w ∈ {c ≤ dens μ} ⊆ sing φ_μ. Then dist(w_j, w) ≥ ε for all j, contradicting w_j → w. Hence there is k₀ with B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_k ⊆ {x : ∃ z ∈ sing φ_μ, dist(x, z) < ε} for all k ≥ k₀.
8. (Application of A.4; parent steps 6, 7.) Hypothesis (ADR), applied to (P, n, Q := 1, F, sing) with the hypotheses verified in step 7, gives (I) or (II).
(I) B_1(0) ∩ sing φ = ∅ for every φ ∈ F. For μ ∈ 𝓜, {x ∈ B_1(0) : c ≤ dens μ x} ⊆ B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_μ = ∅, which is the first alternative.
(II) There is d with d + 1 ≤ n such that μH[d + α](sing φ ∩ B_1(0)) = 0 for φ ∈ F and α > 0; if d = 0, sing φ ∩ B_σ(0) is finite for φ ∈ F and σ < 1; and there are ψ ∈ F and L with dim L = d, sing ψ = L and ψ(y + λx) = ψ(x) for y ∈ L, λ > 0. For μ ∈ 𝓜, {x ∈ B_1(0) : c ≤ dens μ x} ⊆ sing φ_μ ∩ B_1(0), so it is μH[d + α]-null by monotonicity. If d = 0, {x ∈ B_σ(0) : c ≤ dens μ x} ⊆ sing φ_μ ∩ B_σ(0) is finite. Write ψ = φ_ν with ν ∈ 𝓜; coordinate 0 gives dens ν (y + λx) = dens ν x for y ∈ L, λ > 0.
Let E := {x : c ≤ dens ν x}, so closure E = L.
– E ⊆ L.
– E ≠ ∅, since otherwise closure ∅ = ∅ ≠ L ∋ 0.
– dens ν is constant on L: for y ∈ L, dens ν y = dens ν (y + 1•0) = dens ν 0.
Taking x₀ ∈ E ⊆ L, we get c ≤ dens ν x₀ = dens ν 0 = dens ν y for all y ∈ L. Hence E = L.
Finally ν(ℝ^P) = ∞. First, ν ≠ 0, since otherwise dens ν ≡ 0 < c and E = ∅. With y = 0, dens ν(λx) = dens ν x. By (2) and Hⁿ(λ·s) = λⁿHⁿ(s), the change of variables x = λx′ gives ν(λ·s) = ∫_{λ·s} ofReal(dens ν) dHⁿ = λⁿ∫_s ofReal(dens ν(λ·)) dHⁿ = λⁿν(s). Choose R₁ with ν(B_{R₁}(0)) > 0, which exists because ν(ℝ^P) = sup_R ν(B_R(0)) > 0. Then ν(B_{tR₁}(0)) = tⁿν(B_{R₁}(0)) → ∞ as t → ∞ (n ≥ 1), so ν(ℝ^P) = ∞. This gives the second alternative with this d, ν and L. ∎

dens μ is Borel (lower semicontinuity in x, left continuity in ρ, rational radii); dens μ^{y,λ} = dens μ(y + λ·), and homogeneous ν have dilation-invariant dens ν.

Verify A.1 (closure (3)), A.2 (hypothesis (4) plus normalized pairings), A.3(1) (c′ < c gives an empty superlevel set; c′ ≥ c gives infinite mass, contradicting (6)), A.3(2) (homeomorphism), and A.3(3) (subsequence argument with Lemma D).

subproblems.statement:
Assume (IM), (MON), (MB) and (TAN). (IM), (MON) and (MB) are, in exactly the form of their frozen Lean types, the statements of Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure, Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity and Submission.dimred_blowup_limit_moving_centres (the three registered dependencies of the selected parent). (TAN) is, verbatim, the conclusion of the sibling child tangent_measure_homogeneous (Submission.dimred_tr_tangent_measure_homogeneous: Simon 7.3.1(2) with the homogeneity of cone weights) after its two leading hypotheses (MON) and (MB):
- (IM): an IMRep of a current on an open domain has M_W = weight on open W, support = support of the weight, and a unique weight.
- (MON): monotonicity (i) with e^{Λρ} on compact sets, (ii) without the factor when N = ℝ^P, existence and upper semicontinuity of densities (iii), and density ≥ 1 on the support (iv) for minimizing currents with ∂T = 0 in an embedded C² submanifold.
- (MB): subsequential weak limits of blow-ups with moving centres x_j → x ∈ U and scales → 0 exist, are minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂ = 0, and carry mass-measure convergence.
- (TAN): for n ≥ 1, T minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U, a point x ∈ spt T and scales λ_j → 0, a subsequence of the blow-ups η_{x,λ_j#}T converges weakly in ℝ^P, with mass-measure convergence, to a current C that is minimizing in ℝ^P and whose IMRep weights are n-homogeneous.
Under these hypotheses: Let n, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≤ k and n ≥ 1, P := n + k, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in U ∩ N with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U. Let z ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0 with B̄_{2r}(z) ⊆ U. For Borel measures μ on ℝ^P let dens μ x := (limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ)).toReal and μ^{y,λ} := ofReal(λ⁻¹ⁿ) • μ.map (dilation y λ). Then there are a set 𝓜 of Borel measures on ℝ^P and Λ ∈ ℝ such that: (1) each μ ∈ 𝓜 is finite on compact sets; (2) each μ ∈ 𝓜 equals Hⁿ.withDensity (ofReal ∘ dens μ), Hⁿ = μHE[n]; (3) μ^{y,λ} ∈ 𝓜 whenever μ ∈ 𝓜, 0 < λ < 1, |y| ≤ 1 − λ; (4) for μ ∈ 𝓜, |y| < 1 and strictly decreasing λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0, there are a strictly increasing sub and ν ∈ 𝓜 with ν(λ·s) = λⁿν(s) (λ > 0, s Borel) and ∫ f dμ^{y,λ_{sub(j)}} → ∫ f dν for every continuous compactly supported f; (5) for μ ∈ 𝓜 and B̄_R(y) ⊆ B̄_2(0), ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·μ(B_ρ(y)) is nondecreasing on (0, R); (6) some μ₀ ∈ 𝓜 has dens μ₀ w = θ whenever |w| < 1 and HasMassDensity T (z + rw) θ; (7) for every ν ∈ 𝓜 with ν(ℝ^P) = ∞ there are S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), points x_i ∈ B_r(z) and scales λ_i > 0 with λ_i → 0 such that η_{x_i,λ_i#}T ⇀ S in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly), S is minimizing in ℝ^P, ∂S = 0, and HasMassDensity S y (dens ν y) for every y ∈ ℝ^P. (In the Lean statement dens is a universally quantified function fixed by its defining equation.)

Source: parent proof, steps 1, 2(a)–(f), 3(i)–(iii) and 3(vii) (Simon's class 𝒯 of rescalings η_{x,λ#}T′ of T′ = (η_{z,r#}T)⌞B_2(0) and their zero-scale limits), stated for the class 𝓜 := {μ_S : (S, U_S) ∈ 𝒯} of extended mass measures.
Sibling lemmas used: imrep_density_ae (Submission.dimred_tr_imrep_density_ae), blowup_calculus (Submission.dimred_tr_blowup_calculus), the reused accepted blowup_imrep (Submission.dtc_blowUp_imrep: for an IMRep R of A ∈ 𝒟_n(O), a point a and t > 0 there is an IMRep R′ of blowUp A a t in dilation a t '' O with R′.measure s = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ)·R.measure(dilation a t ⁻¹' s) for every Borel s; no hypothesis on O or n), and iterated_blowup_limit (Submission.dimred_tr_iterated_blowup_limit). Hypotheses (IM), (MON), (MB), (TAN): the first three leading hypotheses of the statement are, verbatim, the frozen Lean types of Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure, Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity and Submission.dimred_blowup_limit_moving_centres (the registered dependencies of the selected parent), and the fourth is, verbatim, the conclusion of the sibling tangent_measure_homogeneous (Submission.dimred_tr_tangent_measure_homogeneous) after its hypotheses (MON) and (MB); the selected parent obtains it by applying that sibling to its registered dependencies. The proof uses these four results only through the hypotheses, at the places where the parent proof cites them (steps 1, 2(b), 2(e), 3(vii)). (IM)(a) gives M_O(A) = R.measure(O) for every IMRep R of a current A on an open domain and every open O inside that domain. (MON)(i), (ii), (iii) give the monotonicity formulas and the existence of densities. (MB) gives minimality and ∂ = 0 of blow-up limits with moving centres. (TAN) gives tangent limits with mass-measure convergence and n-homogeneous weights (parent 2(e) and 3(vii)). No other result outside the sibling set is used.
Notation: P := n + k; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; ω_n := unitBallVolume n; q(μ, x, ρ) := μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ); η_{a,t} := dilation a t, η_{a,t}(p) = t⁻¹(p − a); m^{y,t} := ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ) • m.map η_{y,t} for a measure m.
Step 0 (preliminaries).
(0a) T is integer multiplicity (part of IsMinimizingIn); fix an IMRep R_T of T and put μ_T := R_T.measure. By (IM)(a), M_O(T) = μ_T(O) for open O ⊆ U.
(0b) W := B_{2r}(z), K := B̄_{2r}(z) ⊆ U compact. μ_T(K) < ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult of R_T. μ_W := μ_T.restrict W is a finite measure.
(0c) Apply (MON) to T with d := n + ℓ (1 ≤ n ≤ n + ℓ ≤ n + k; the other hypotheses are those of T). By (i) for K there is Λ_K ≥ 0 such that t ↦ ofReal(e^{Λ_Kt}/tⁿ)·M_{B_t(c′)}(T) is nondecreasing on (0, R′) whenever B̄_{R′}(c′) ⊆ K. Put Λ := rΛ_K.
(0d) ℝ^P is an embedded C² (n+k)-dimensional submanifold: IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + k) univ, witnessed at each point by V = W = ℝ^P and ψ = id (open, smooth, injective, ψ(V) = W ∩ ℝ^P, preimages of compact sets compact, Dψ = id injective). Also (closure univ ∖ univ) ∩ univ = ∅. Hence for S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂S = 0, (MON) applies with U = N = ℝ^P and d = n + k, and (TAN) applies with ℓ := k and U = N = ℝ^P (univ ∩ univ = univ, IsOpen univ, spt S ⊆ univ).
(0e) (Use of (TAN).) Step 7 applies (TAN) in two ways, always with the standing hypothesis n ≥ 1 of the statement. It applies (TAN) to T itself, with its own U and N; ∂T = 0 in U is a hypothesis. It also applies (TAN) to zero-scale currents S ∈ 𝒯₀, with ℓ := k and U = N = ℝ^P via (0d); ∂S = 0 by step 2. No information about spt ∂ is needed, since (TAN) assumes ∂ = 0 directly.
(0f) Uniqueness of weak limits: if ConvergesWeakly (A_i) S and ConvergesWeakly (A_{φ(j)}) C with S, C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and φ strictly increasing, then S = C, because S(ω) and C(ω) are limits of the same subsequence of currentEval(A_i, ω) (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
(0g) The IMRep R_∅ of ℝ^P with empty carrier (multiplicity 0, orientation 0) represents the zero current, and R_∅.measure = 0. Every field holds trivially; the a.e. fields refer to Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0.
(0h) Vanishing blow-ups: suppose A ∈ 𝒟_n(O) vanishes on an open set containing B_ε(p) (A.VanishesOn) and t_j > 0, t_j → 0. Then ConvergesWeakly (blowUp A p t_j) 0. Indeed, for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{R_ω}(0), blowup_calculus (ii) gives currentEval(blowUp A p t_j, ω) = currentEval(A, η_{p,t_j}^#ω), and tsupport η_{p,t_j}^#ω = η_{p,t_j}⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ B_{t_jR_ω}(p) ⊆ B_ε(p) once t_jR_ω < ε. This value is 0 (by VanishesOn if the form lies in 𝒟ⁿ(O), and by definition of currentEval otherwise). If p ∈ O ∖ spt A, such ε exists because p ∈ A.zeroRegion; then M_{B_ε(p)}(A) = 0 and, when A has an IMRep R, R.measure(B_ε(p)) = 0 ((IM)(a)).
(0i) (Homogeneous tangent weights; parent 3(vii).) In step 7, n-homogeneity of the weights of the tangent limits C is part of the conclusion of (TAN). For every IMRep R_C of C, every λ > 0 and every Borel s, R_C.measure(λ·s) = ofReal(λⁿ)·R_C.measure(s), where λ·s = (fun x ↦ λ • x) '' s.
(0j) If R is an IMRep of A ∈ 𝒟_n(O) with O open, p ∈ O and HasMassDensity A p θ, then dens R.measure p = θ. For small ρ, B_ρ(p) ⊆ O and M_{B_ρ(p)}(A) = R.measure(B_ρ(p)), so q(R.measure, p, ρ) → ofReal θ; the limsup equals ofReal θ, and θ ≥ 0.
(0k) Parameter congruence: if a = a′ and t = t′ (t ≠ 0), then currentEval(blowUp A a t h, ω) = currentEval(blowUp A a′ t′ h′, ω) for every form ω. Likewise, ConvergesWeakly and MassMeasuresConverge statements about sequences of blow-ups are unchanged when centres and scales are replaced by pointwise-equal expressions: substitute the equal parameters, the proof arguments being propositions. This is used tacitly below whenever centres and scales are rewritten, e.g. z + r•(x_i + λ_i•y) = (z + r•x_i) + (rλ_i)•y and r(λ_iλ′) = (rλ_i)λ′.
(0l) Measure form of blowup_imrep. Let R be an IMRep of A ∈ 𝒟_n(O), a ∈ ℝ^P and t > 0. blowup_imrep gives an IMRep R′ of blowUp A a t with R′.measure = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ) • R.measure.map (dilation a t). Indeed, dilation a t is continuous, hence measurable. For Borel s, (ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ) • R.measure.map (dilation a t))(s) = ofReal(t⁻¹ⁿ)·R.measure(dilation a t ⁻¹' s) (Measure.smul_apply, Measure.map_apply), and this equals R′.measure(s). Both sides are measures on the Borel σ-algebra, so they are equal (Measure.ext).
Step 1 (the class; parent step 2).
(1a) Positive-scale members (parent 2(a)): for (x, λ) with 0 < λ ≤ 1 and |x| ≤ 1 − λ, put s := rλ, c := z + rx and μ_{x,λ} := ofReal(s⁻¹ⁿ) • μ_W.map η_{c,s}. This is the extended mass measure of η_{x,λ#}T′. For Borel B, μ_{x,λ}(B) = s^{−n}μ_W(η_{c,s}⁻¹B), and η_{c,s}⁻¹(B_ρ(w)) = B_{sρ}(c + sw).
(1b) Zero-scale currents 𝒯₀ (parent 2, parameter λ = 0): S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) belongs to 𝒯₀ if there are x_i ∈ ℝ^P, λ_i ∈ (0, 1) and x̄ ∈ ℝ^P with |x_i| < 1 − λ_i, λ_i → 0, x_i → x̄, and blowUp T (z + r x_i) (rλ_i) ⇀ S in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly). (The current η_{x_i,λ_i#}T′ of the parent agrees with this blow-up of T on η_{x_i,λ_i}(B_2(0)) ⊇ B_{1/λ_i}(0).) Note |x̄| ≤ 1.
(1c) 𝓜₀ := {R.measure : R an IMRep of ℝ^P representing some S ∈ 𝒯₀}, and 𝓜 := {μ_{x,λ}} ∪ 𝓜₀.
Step 2 (zero-scale members are minimizing; parent 2(b)). Let S ∈ 𝒯₀ with data (x_i, λ_i, x̄). Then z + r x̄ ∈ B̄_r(z) ⊆ U, z + r x_i → z + r x̄, and rλ_i → 0. (MB) gives a strictly increasing φ and C with blowUp T (z + rx_{φ(j)}) (rλ_{φ(j)}) ⇀ C, C minimizing in ℝ^P and ∂C = 0. By (0f), S = C. So S is minimizing in ℝ^P, in particular integer multiplicity with IMReps, and ∂S = 0.
Step 3 (local finiteness; property (1)). μ_{x,λ}(ℝ^P) = s^{−n}μ_T(W) < ∞. For R.measure ∈ 𝓜₀ (R an IMRep of ℝ^P) and compact K, R.measure(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult (K ⊆ ℝ^P).
Step 4 (density representation, property (2); parent 3(iii)).
(4a) Let R.measure ∈ 𝓜₀. Apply imrep_density_ae to R with W := ℝ^P; finiteness holds by step 3. For Hⁿ-a.e. x, q(R.measure, x, ρ) → g(x) := 1_M(x)θ(x) < ∞. So, for Hⁿ-a.e. x, dens R.measure x = g(x).toReal and ofReal(dens R.measure x) = g(x). Hence Hⁿ.withDensity(ofReal∘dens R.measure) = Hⁿ.withDensity(1_Mθ) = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ = R.measure (withDensity_congr_ae, withDensity_indicator).
(4b) Apply imrep_density_ae to R_T with the open set W. Finiteness: R_T.measure(K′ ∩ W) ≤ μ_T(K) < ∞ for compact K′. For Hⁿ-a.e. p, q(μ_W, p, ρ) = R_T.measure(B_ρ(p) ∩ W)/(ω_nρⁿ) → g_W(p), where g_W := 1_{M_T∩W}·θ_T is a Borel function with finite values; hence ofReal(dens μ_W p) = g_W(p) for Hⁿ-a.e. p. Also μ_W = (Hⁿ⌞(M_T ∩ W)).withDensity θ_T = Hⁿ.withDensity g_W (withDensity_indicator; M_T ∩ W is Borel).
(4c) Let μ_{x,λ}, with s, c as in (1a) and η := η_{c,s}. Since η is a measurable equivalence and g_W is measurable, μ_W.map η = (Hⁿ.withDensity g_W).map η = (Hⁿ.map η).withDensity(g_W∘η⁻¹); evaluate both sides on Borel sets with lintegral_map_equiv. Also Hⁿ.map η = sⁿ·Hⁿ, since Hⁿ(η⁻¹B) = Hⁿ(c + sB) = sⁿHⁿ(B) by translation invariance and homogeneity of μHE[n]. Hence μ_{x,λ} = Hⁿ.withDensity(g_W∘η⁻¹). By (1a), q(μ_{x,λ}, w, ρ) = q(μ_W, c + sw, sρ), so (as ρ ↦ sρ preserves 𝓝[>]0) dens μ_{x,λ} w = dens μ_W (c + sw) = dens μ_W (η⁻¹w) for every w. Since η maps Hⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets (Hⁿ(η(Z)) = s^{−n}Hⁿ(Z)), (4b) gives ofReal(dens μ_{x,λ} w) = g_W(η⁻¹w) for Hⁿ-a.e. w. By withDensity_congr_ae, μ_{x,λ} = Hⁿ.withDensity(ofReal∘dens μ_{x,λ}), which proves (2) for μ_{x,λ}. No measurability of dens μ_W or dens μ_{x,λ} is needed, since withDensity_congr_ae only uses Hⁿ-a.e. equality.
Step 5 (closure under rescaling, property (3); parent 2(c)). Let 0 < λ′ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ′.
(5a) For μ_{x,λ}: ofReal(λ′⁻¹ⁿ) • μ_{x,λ}.map η_{y,λ′} = ofReal((sλ′)⁻¹ⁿ) • μ_W.map(η_{y,λ′}∘η_{c,s}) (Measure.map_smul, Measure.map_map). Also η_{y,λ′}∘η_{c,s} = η_{c+sy, sλ′}, since λ′⁻¹(s⁻¹(p − c) − y) = (sλ′)⁻¹(p − c − sy). Here c + sy = z + r(x + λy) and sλ′ = r(λλ′). So the rescaled measure is μ_{x+λy, λλ′}, and the pair is admissible: 0 < λλ′ ≤ 1 and |x + λy| ≤ 1 − λ + λ(1 − λ′) = 1 − λλ′. The same computation shows μ_{x,λ}^{y,t} = ofReal((st)⁻¹ⁿ) • μ_W.map η_{c+sy, st} for every t > 0.
(5b) For ν = R.measure ∈ 𝓜₀, with R representing S ∈ 𝒯₀ with data (x_i, λ_i, x̄):
– (0l) gives an IMRep R′ of blowUp S y λ′, a current on η_{y,λ′}(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P, with R′.measure = ofReal(λ′⁻¹ⁿ) • ν.map η_{y,λ′}.
– Let S′ := (blowUp S y λ′).restrictDomain (ℝ^P ⊆ η_{y,λ′}(ℝ^P)) ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), and let R″ be the IMRep of ℝ^P with the same carrier, multiplicity and orientation as R′. The IMRep axioms refer to the domain only through "carrier ⊆ domain" and "compact ⊆ domain", and the two domains are equal sets. R″ represents S′, and R″.measure = R′.measure.
– S′ ∈ 𝒯₀ with data x′_i := x_i + λ_iy, λ′_i := λ_iλ′ and x̄: λ′_i ∈ (0, 1), |x′_i| < 1 − λ_i + λ_i(1 − λ′) = 1 − λ′_i, λ′_i → 0 and x′_i → x̄. Put a_i := z + rx_i and t_i := rλ_i; then z + rx′_i = a_i + t_iy and rλ′_i = t_iλ′. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), blowup_calculus (iii) then (ii) give currentEval(blowUp T (z + rx′_i) (rλ′_i), ω) = currentEval(blowUp T a_i t_i, η_{y,λ′}^#ω) → S(η_{y,λ′}^#ω) = currentEval(blowUp S y λ′, ω) = S′(ω).
Hence ofReal(λ′⁻¹ⁿ) • ν.map η_{y,λ′} = R″.measure ∈ 𝓜₀.
Step 6 (monotonicity, property (5); parent 2(a), 2(b)). Let B̄_R(y) ⊆ B̄_2(0) and ρ ∈ (0, R); if R ≤ 0 there is nothing to prove. For R > 0 we have |y| + R ≤ 2: since P = n + k ≥ 1, there is a unit vector u with y = |y|u (any unit vector if y = 0), and y + Ru lies in B̄_R(y) ⊆ B̄_2(0) and has norm |y| + R.
(6a) For μ_{x,λ}, put c′ := c + sy = z + r(x + λy). Then |c′ − z| + sR = r(|x + λy| + λR) ≤ r(1 − λ + λ(|y| + R)) ≤ r(1 + λ) ≤ 2r. So B̄_{sR}(c′) ⊆ K and B_{sρ}(c′) ⊆ W, and μ_{x,λ}(B_ρ(y)) = s^{−n}μ_T(B_{sρ}(c′)) = s^{−n}M_{B_{sρ}(c′)}(T) by (0a). By (0c), t ↦ ofReal(e^{Λ_Kt}/tⁿ)M_{B_t(c′)}(T) is nondecreasing on (0, sR). So G(ρ) := ofReal(e^{sΛ_Kρ}/ρⁿ)·μ_{x,λ}(B_ρ(y)), which is that function at t = sρ, is nondecreasing on (0, R). Then ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·μ_{x,λ}(B_ρ(y)) = ofReal(e^{(r−s)Λ_Kρ})·G(ρ) is a product of two nonnegative nondecreasing functions (r − s = r(1 − λ) ≥ 0 and Λ_K ≥ 0), hence nondecreasing.
(6b) For ν = R.measure ∈ 𝓜₀ with R representing S ∈ 𝒯₀: by step 2 and (0d), (MON)(ii) applies to S with N = ℝ^P. So ρ ↦ ofReal(1/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(S) = ofReal(1/ρⁿ)·ν(B_ρ(y)) ((IM)(a)) is nondecreasing on (0, R) for every R. Multiplying by the nondecreasing factor ofReal(e^{Λρ}) (Λ ≥ 0) keeps it nondecreasing.
Step 7 (tangent measures, property (4); parent 2(e)). Let μ ∈ 𝓜, |y| < 1, and λ_j > 0 strictly decreasing to 0.
(7a) μ = μ_{x,λ}. By (5a), μ^{y,t} = ofReal((st)⁻¹ⁿ) • μ_W.map η_{p, st} for t > 0, where p := c + sy = z + r(x + λy). Since |x + λy| ≤ 1 − λ + λ|y| < 1, p ∈ B_r(z) ⊆ U and B_r(p) ⊆ W.
Case p ∈ spt T. Apply (TAN) to T at p (∂T = 0 in U; see (0e)) with the sequence t_j := sλ_j. It gives a strictly increasing φ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with blowUp T p (sλ_{φ(j)}) ⇀ C, MassMeasuresConverge, C minimizing in ℝ^P, and n-homogeneous weights for every IMRep of C. Let R_C be an IMRep of C (C is integer multiplicity, being minimizing) and ν := R_C.measure.
(i) ν ∈ 𝓜₀. Choose j₀ with λλ_{φ(j)} < 1 − |x + λy| for j ≥ j₀. The data x′_j := x + λy, λ′_j := λλ_{φ(j+j₀)}, x̄ := x + λy satisfy the conditions of 𝒯₀. Moreover blowUp T (z + rx′_j) (rλ′_j) = blowUp T p (sλ_{φ(j+j₀)}) ⇀ C, as a tail of a convergent sequence.
(ii) ν is homogeneous by (TAN); see (0i).
(iii) Vague convergence. Let R_j be the IMRep of blowUp T p (sλ_{φ(j)}) given by (0l) from R_T, with R_j.measure = ofReal((sλ_{φ(j)})⁻¹ⁿ) • μ_T.map η_{p, sλ_{φ(j)}}. MassMeasuresConverge gives ∫ f dR_j.measure → ∫ f dν for continuous compactly supported f. If tsupport f ⊆ B_{R_f}(0) and sλ_{φ(j)}R_f < r, then f∘η_{p,sλ_{φ(j)}} is supported in B_{sλ_{φ(j)}R_f}(p) ⊆ W. Hence ∫ f dμ^{y,λ_{φ(j)}} = ∫ f dR_j.measure: both equal (sλ_{φ(j)})^{−n}∫ f∘η dμ_T, by integral_smul_measure, integral_map, and the agreement of μ_W and μ_T on subsets of W.
